rule: Build interaction prototypes directly in code before design tools to discover constraints and happy accidents.
quote: If you have an idea for a chair, you don't just draw pictures—you build prototypes out of wood or plastic. The material reveals strengths and limitations that shape the idea. With software, the material is code.

rule: Ensure text contrast meets minimum ratios: 4.5:1 for small text, 3.0:1 for large text.
quote: The web accessibility guidelines suggest a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5 for small text, and 3.0 for large text.

rule: Implement undo by preserving the principle: copy-undo-redo should not change the document if others edited in between.
quote: If you undo a lot, copy something, and redo back to the present (a common operation), the document should not change.

rule: Broadcast user changes to the server and all clients in real-time to keep shared state current.
quote: Changes from each user are sent up to the server and broadcast to other users in real-time.

rule: Provide text alternatives for all non-text content so users can perceive it in their preferred format.
quote: Provide text alternatives for any non-text content so that it can be changed into other forms people need, such as large print, braille, speech, symbols or simpler language.

rule: Label all controls and input elements with names that describe their purpose.
quote: If non-text content is a control or accepts user input, then it has a name that describes its purpose.

rule: Implement decorative images so assistive technology can ignore them.
quote: If non-text content is pure decoration, is used only for visual formatting, or is not presented to users, then it is implemented in a way that it can be ignored by assistive technology.

rule: Guide primary navigation through a sidebar instead of a horizontal top bar for faster visual scanning.
quote: information displayed in vertical layouts allows for faster visual processing - the eye reads lists faster than it can scan horizontally

rule: Create separate visual containers for distinct user workflows rather than flat grouping within a single interface.
quote: creating a separate surface such that these idea spaces become distinct environments, rather than joined tabs within an existing instance

rule: Respond to user input within 50ms; treat this as a hard engineering constraint, not a guideline.
quote: Users perceive any latency above 50ms; treat this as a hard engineering constraint, not a guideline
finding: 50ms threshold for perceived latency

rule: Display keyboard shortcuts inline in results, not hidden in tooltips or documentation.
quote: Show shortcuts inline (not in tooltips)

rule: Add delight through small personality touches without incurring performance cost.
quote: Personality without performance cost - Confetti on achievements, playful empty states, and clever copy create delight without adding latency

rule: Create memorable and engaging experiences by using interaction details that surprise and delight users.
quote: provide memorable, engaging, and satisfying experiences enhanced by Apple technologies

rule: Design interfaces that reflect diverse backgrounds, abilities, and languages to serve all users equally.
quote: provide a great experience for all by reflecting a variety of backgrounds, abilities, and languages

rule: Make undo easy and freely available so users can recover confidently from their mistakes.
quote: You can provide forgiveness by making it easy for them to undo any of their actions.

rule: Ask for personal data only at the right moment with context, not on app launch before users understand the app.
quote: Responsible interfaces wait for the right moment to ask for personal data. They only ask for what's necessary, and are transparent about the data is for.

rule: Let users explore your product at their own pace; avoid forcing them down a predetermined path.
quote: Instead of guiding someone down a pre-determined path, let them dive right into your experience. And give them the autonomy to decide what to explore at their own pace.

rule: Speed and quality correlate positively; expertise enables fast iteration without cutting corners.
quote: Speed and quality aren't actually at odds—they're often positively correlated. The best practitioners in any field, from chefs to programmers, work quickly because they're experts.

rule: Explore extreme versions of a feature—fastest and safest—then converge toward a balanced solution.
quote: What's the most extreme version of this idea? For example, instead of trying to figure out a perfect draft-saving feature, ask, "What's the fastest version we could do? What's the safest?"

rule: Translate all visual information into text; test designs with screen readers for blind users.
quote: Is visual information translated effectively into text? Can the image be understood through its metadata alone? When possible, test all designs through a screen reader.

rule: Provide captions and transcripts for all videos and animations with meaningful audio.
quote: Find an alternative way to convey information exclusively with sound. Transcribe and caption all videos and animations that have meaningful audio.

rule: When users expect high-stakes outcomes (money, migration, analysis), make processes appear appropriately effortful rather than suspiciously instant.
quote: People dislike waiting in general, but if your users have high expectations (e.g., money transaction, migration, analysis, reporting), they become skeptical if the waiting time is too short.

rule: Use familiar interface elements like sidebars, tabs, and search fields so people recognize and know how to use them on spatial platforms.
quote: Common elements like sidebars, tabs, and search fields help people find the music they're looking for.

rule: Design windows with glass material to provide contrast with the world and give people awareness of their surroundings.
quote: The glass material provides contrast with the world, gives people more awareness of their surroundings, and adapts to different lighting conditions.

rule: Ensure windows always turn to face the user when moved to keep interfaces easy to read and use.
quote: Notice how they always turn to face someone when moving. This keeps interfaces easy to read and easy to use.

rule: Keep your app interface in a single window; multiple windows can quickly become overwhelming for users to manage.
quote: Ideally, keep your app's interface in a single window. Multiple windows can quickly become a lot for people to manage.

rule: Use points to specify interface element sizes so they scale correctly as windows move closer or farther from the user.
quote: as people move windows, they scale larger as they move away and scale smaller as they move closer to them. This keeps interfaces legible and usable.

rule: Use copy that directly aligns with the actual offer, not patterns users associate with selling.
quote: A CTA aligned with the offer and without 'decline' options.

rule: Use stories to engage multiple brain areas and make content more memorable than statistics alone.
quote: Stories engage with multiple areas of the brain, making stories more memorable than simple facts and statistics alone.

rule: Make content simple, unexpected, concrete, emotional, and story-driven to help ideas stick.
quote: Simple (very short and basic) Unexpected (curiosity gap) Concrete (e.g. relevant to COVID19) Emotional (fun/fear, music-driven) Story (e.g. woman looking for a mask)

rule: Design apps to work for people with disabilities, expanding reach and sparking creative innovation.
quote: When you include disability into your design, you'll make your app work for more people and also spark more creativity.

rule: Support multiple interaction types so users can interact with your app using different senses and abilities.
quote: Find out how to make your apps more inclusive by supporting multiple types of interaction, providing customization, and adopting accessibility APIs.

rule: Recognize that disability emerges from gaps between abilities and environmental design; close these gaps.
quote: When there's a difference between what a person can actually do and what society expects, that is where disability is really born.

rule: Make UI and interactions obvious and unspoken so users focus on their task, not the interface.
quote: That should all be obvious, and blatantly unspoken, and just completely in the background.

rule: Remind users of the core benefit they sought during first use.
quote: Users come to your app with a specific intent. Always remind them why they should use your app during their first experience.

rule: Never use fake scarcity or false urgency in onboarding.
quote: Never use this pattern if you fake the scarce!

rule: Repeat stimulus less frequently and vary presentation to prevent habituation.
quote: The more a stimulus is repeated, the less intense your reaction will be.

rule: Build trust by explaining why you need data before asking for it.
quote: Build trust before you ask for data. And explain clearly why you need it.

rule: Deliver value before requesting major commitments; users reciprocate after experiencing benefits.
quote: Users are more likely to engage with your product after you provide value.

rule: Highlight quick wins in onboarding to prevent users from missing important accomplishments.
quote: this was so quick that I almost missed it.

rule: Use visual priming with product images to help users recall information and increase conversion.
quote: Subtle visual suggestions help users recall specific information, influencing how they respond.

rule: Simplify experience for new and returning users by reducing difficulty to boost activation and retention.
quote: Try to offer a "simplified" experience with reduced difficulty, even if you have to cheat your user flows a bit.

rule: Make intrusive or risky actions as transparent as possible to users.
quote: the more intrusive or risky an action is, the more transparent they should be about it

rule: Minimize effort required for users to take action they intend to take.
quote: We are more likely to take action when the effort is small

rule: Reassure users immediately after purchase to maintain trust and satisfaction.
quote: Not reassuring people after a purchase can leave them uneasy — damaging trust at the very start of the relationship

rule: Help users recognize context rather than forcing them to recall it from previous steps.
quote: It's easier for people to recognize something shown on screen than to recall it from memory

rule: Design products for users first, not advertisers; resolve conflicts between revenue and user experience.
quote: Teams optimize for money, while the experience for real users deteriorates.

rule: Limit choices to reduce decision fatigue; presenting four options for one interaction causes hesitation and confusion.
quote: The more choices you present to someone, the more time it takes for them to decide.

rule: Make permission requests low-friction micro-commitments coherent with the user's previous actions, not big asks.
quote: People feel less threatened by small steps that are coherent with your previous actions.

rule: Avoid manipulating users; trust erodes when deception is perceived.
quote: When we believe we are being manipulated, we develop an intense emotional response resulting from a perceived encroachment on our intelligence and trust.

rule: Frame skipping onboarding steps as losing personalization to increase perceived value.
quote: Grammarly reframed skipping questions as "skipping personalization" to make users value every step more.

rule: Show contextual guidance at the moment of need, not all instructions upfront.
quote: Make sure you show the right message to the right user at the right time. Rather than asking your users to remember everything up-front, you should provide guidance as they go.

rule: Start with simple actions before complex ones to avoid overwhelming users.
quote: Encouraging users to move from completing simple actions to executing more complex ones lowers the chances that users will feel overwhelmed.

rule: Design interfaces to match users' existing mental models based on real-world experiences and past interactions.
quote: mental models are how people think something works

rule: Design online interactions to follow social norms and rules users expect in person-to-person interactions.
quote: People expect most online interactions to follow the same social rules as person-to-person interactions

rule: Use familiar patterns and visuals to help users understand new features faster; wrap unfamiliar concepts in familiar design.
quote: When introducing a new feature or product, try using existing patterns and visuals to help people understand faster

rule: Provide gentle reminders or cues when users attempt familiar actions that no longer apply in your product to help them migrate mental models.
quote: a gentle reminder when they press ⌘ S would be a great start

rule: Build momentum by asking users to agree to small, easy tasks before making larger asks.
quote: People are more likely to agree to a large task after saying yes to a smaller one

rule: Outline step-by-step plans clearly to reassure users and motivate them through critical funnel steps.
quote: Clearly outlining the next steps reassures and motivates people

rule: Reduce the number of response options to ease decision-making; 11 options (0-10) add complexity without improving accuracy.
quote: The effort needed to make a decision increases with the number of options

rule: Avoid relying on NPS as a one-size-fits-all metric; use it purposefully rather than as a blanket measurement.
quote: Companies are too obsessed with Net Promoter Scores. They blindly use NPS as a one-size-fits-all solution. That creates a spam nightmare

rule: Build design skills through repeated exposure to use cases so you can recognize patterns and anticipate design problems.
quote: The more use cases you see, the better you get at recognizing patterns

rule: Break complex designs into simple composable building blocks connected in a creative pipeline.
quote: break down complex designs and use a creative pipeline to chain simple building blocks together

rule: Each graphics modifier or API is a stage in a data transformation pipeline; connect them to layer effects.
quote: every modifier, every API, is another stage in the pipeline. It just flows

rule: Go beyond text in select options by using the ::selectedcontent element for rich content display.
quote: With customizable select, I can now go beyond the simple list of options displayed as text

rule: Name features by what they do for users, not by technology or internal function.
quote: it's natural to name it by what it does, the technology behind it, or the function. But the people using your app don't see it that way. They want to know what it does for them

rule: Arrange heterogeneous content in a single dimension with automatic column distribution, not a rigid grid.
quote: Grid Lanes distributes content across multiple lanes. The result is a tightly packed, staggered layout that preserves each item's natural proportions.

rule: Let the browser compute column count and size with auto-fill and minmax() rather than forcing a fixed layout.
quote: Instead of picking the number of columns yourself, let the browser decide. auto-fill creates as many columns as will fit. minmax() says each one should be at least 200 pixels, but can grow to fill the space.

rule: Make the iOS tab bar reserve prominent space for a single key action, distinguishing it from content tabs.
quote: The shopping cart tab is displayed on the bottom trailing edge of the screen, distinguishing it from the other tabs, which contain store content. To enable this special tab placement, I'm using the new prominent tab role to make it stand out.

rule: Mark custom interactive elements as responsive to user input so they feel fluid under mouse or touch.
quote: On macOS, like on iOS, you can mark Liquid Glass custom elements as 'interactive' so they respond more fluidly to user's clicks. And this is optimized to work great with the mouse pointer, so it feels right at home on the Mac.

rule: Visualize your environment in layers from background to foreground during planning to reduce production complications.
quote: Try to visualize your environment in terms of layers, building from the background to the foreground. Identify which scene elements will need to have motion, and start thinking about what spatial audio you can attach to them.

rule: Use native components (tab bars, toolbars, context menus) for functional UI; only customize for high-impact areas.
quote: Custom components take refinement. So you should focus your time building them for areas of your app that have the biggest impact or make your content stand out. Then, audit your app for opportunities to use standard components for aspects of your app that are functional.

rule: Lean on platform-familiar interaction patterns so users instinctively know how to use your app.
quote: Establishing a baseline of platform familiarity is important. Otherwise people will need to learn how to use your app. Standard components such as grid views and grouped tables are highly flexible and functional. If you draw upon what people already understand, they'll instinctively know how to use your app.

rule: Test icons across the system-wide transparency slider to ensure legibility at all opacity levels.
quote: Does the new Icon Composer let us preview across the system-wide transparency slider — and what's the guidance when a clear-mode icon fails contrast at a user's extreme?

rule: Use opacity and blend modes deliberately in Liquid Glass icons to create depth and physical presence.
quote: How do you give a flat 2D brand mark a convincing physical presence in Liquid Glass?

rule: Avoid washed-out tint-mode backgrounds; adjust settings to achieve better color vibrancy and contrast.
quote: In tint mode, background colors look washed out and lack contrast. Any advice on settings to achieve better vibrancy?

rule: Leverage word-of-mouth credibility; consumers are more likely to buy on peer recommendation.
quote: Group Nielsen found that consumers were 77% more likely to buy a product if their friends recommended it.
finding: 77 percent more likely to buy on friend recommendation

rule: Avoid panic-inducing countdown timers that rush users without breathing room.
quote: Temu uses multiple countdown timers to create urgency the moment you enter the app — giving people little breathing room to explore.

rule: Leverage loss aversion carefully; fear of losing rewards can nudge irrational spending.
quote: Temu leverages our fear of losing the £100 to nudge us to make irrational spending decisions.

rule: Set defaults that align with user values and product ethics; most users keep the default and avoid friction.
quote: Every choice has a default. Doing nothing is a default. And people are more likely to keep things the way they are – maintaining the status quo and not take action to change things.

rule: Place high-recall items first or last in lists; people remember endpoints better than middle items.
quote: We have much better recall of the first and last items within a list.

rule: Use visual anchors to reinforce loss aversion; an overflowing bar alerts better than text alone.
quote: Using a visual anchor to reinforce loss aversion (e.g. illustration, progress bar) is a great way to maximize the engagement rate of your users.

rule: Study the Human Interface Guidelines alongside design resources to understand when and why to use each component.
quote: looking at the Apple Human Interface Guidelines in tandem with the design resources is really, really beneficial because we have so much information about where and when and why to use different components

rule: Move controls to the side of the outer display to maximize vertical space for content.
quote: Buttons and controls that normally sit at the top and bottom move to the right side of the display in order to maximize vertical space and to make them easier to reach

rule: Shift text and images away from the center fold when device is partially folded to ensure readability.
quote: When that happens, content automatically moves away from the center region. Text and images shift away from the curve so they are easier to read.

rule: Use layout margins and horizontal safe area insets instead of fixed widths or breakpoints for responsive design.
quote: Build your layouts with layout margins and horizontal safe area insets. If you're already using these tools, you're off to a great start.

rule: Design apps to be freely resizable rather than tied to specific screen sizes or poses.
quote: design your app to be freely resizable and you'll be in good shape

rule: Do not tie app functionality to specific device poses; ensure all controls exist in every pose.
quote: You don't want to tie functionality to a specific pose.

rule: Use displacement patterns to keep important content visible and reachable when device folds.
quote: displacement, which adjusts the frame of the existing elements based on the available space, keeping important content visible, reachable, and unobstructed even when the device is partially folded

rule: Move related elements together to preserve their visual relationship during displacement.
quote: When elements work together, move them together to preserve their relationship. And remember to be mindful of excessive movement.

rule: Do not displace continuous scrolling content like articles, feeds, and lists.
quote: Continuous scrolling content like articles, feeds, documents, and lists don't displace. These experiences already adapt through scrolling, so moving them between the available regions can interrupt continuity.

rule: Move navigation, toolbar, and tab bar controls to the side on iPhone Duo's outer display to preserve vertical space.
quote: To make the most out of that width and preserve vertical space for content, controls that normally sit at the top and bottom, move to the side, where they're also easier to reach.

rule: Rebuild apps against the latest iOS SDK to opt into vertical bar layout on iPhone Duo.
quote: To opt your app into the new bar behavior, there are a few things you'll need to do. First, rebuild your app against the latest SDKs.

rule: Use standard navigation containers like NavigationStack or TabView instead of custom bars.
quote: Next, make sure you're using the bars provided by navigation containers like TabView or NavigationStack.

rule: Order toolbar items vertically with primary navigation at top, followed by prominent actions.
quote: When displayed vertically, items retain a clear top-to-bottom hierarchy. Start by auditing your existing toolbar configuration, making sure that controls follow the recommended order. Reserve the top for primary navigation controls, like back or close, followed by prominent actions, such as done.

rule: Prefer symbol-only items in vertical bars to conserve space.
quote: Prefer symbol-only items

rule: Use size classes instead of interface orientation to make layout decisions.
quote: Avoid checking interface orientation for layout decisions. Use size classes instead.

rule: Avoid referencing the main screen; use environment, trait collection, or scene bounds instead.
quote: avoid referencing the main screen in your code. It's ambiguous and will be deprecated in a future release. If possible, don't use screen references at all. Instead, use more local concepts like the environment, trait collection, or the scene's bounds.

rule: Use Concentricity APIs to ensure UI fits perfectly in corners on curved displays.
quote: To make sure your UI fits the corners of the screen perfectly, use Concentricity APIs introduced in iOS 26. They're updated to work with the screen shapes on iPhone Duo.

rule: Build apps with flexible layouts that adapt across a continuum of sizes instead of assuming fixed dimensions.
quote: The best app layouts are adaptive across a continuum of devices. They avoid making assumptions about display sizes or device capabilities based on user interface idioms.

rule: Enlarge UI components on Apple Watch Series 7 to make full use of the expanded content area.
quote: We enlarged UI components to make full use of the additional space for enhanced usability.

rule: Use large titles in watchOS to improve glanceability and establish clearer hierarchy.
quote: We brought large titles into watchOS this year to make apps more glanceable, offer a better sense of place, and establish clearer hierarchy within apps.

rule: Apply scenePadding modifier only to text content that would distort or be clipped by edges.
quote: Try to preserve using the .scenePadding modifier only for text content that would distort or be clipped by the edges of the display.

rule: Use color strategically for wayfinding, hierarchy, and app identity on watch interfaces.
quote: Color is meant to help with wayfinding, information hierarchy, and signal the personality of your app.

rule: Layer visual elements by depth to create a sense of dimension and physical presence in app icons.
quote: The material layers different elements like edge highlights, frostiness, and translucency to not only add a sense of depth

rule: Use translucency and frostiness effects to make icons appear lit from within and enhance visual expressiveness.
quote: it really makes it seem as if the icons are lit from within. And adding to this physicality, the material comes alive

rule: Use unified grid-based design across platforms to maintain visual consistency while supporting multiple device formats.
quote: we've now made it easier to design across our devices for both rounded rectangle and circle formats. Let's start with our rounded rectangle shape. We've updated the design grid to a simpler and more evenly spaced structure.

rule: Use vector formats like SVG for icon design to ensure maximum scalability across different sizes and resolutions.
quote: it's best to use a tool that can draw in vectors since having the ability to export SVGs will give you the most scalability

rule: Structure icons with distinct layers representing depth to enable dynamic material effects like glass properties and lighting.
quote: each layer represents a step in Z depth, where the bottom is the background and the other stack on top

rule: Use variable typefaces with continuous scaling for weight, width, and corner softness to enable rich customization without limiting to preset styles.
quote: Our variable fonts allow qualities like weight and width both extended and condensed as well as the softness of the corners to all exist on a continuous scale

rule: Enable search across multiple words and their proximity clusters to help users navigate large codebases effectively.
quote: I can enter a set of words. For example, here, I'm trying to find where in my project I'm creating clipped resizable images. Xcode will now find all the clusters of these words in proximity to each other

rule: Avoid auto-restoring transient UI elements like welcome screens, context-dependent tools, or one-time actions when relaunching an app.
quote: Consider disabling scene restoration for transient elements like a welcome screen, context-dependent UI like a tools window tied to a specific app state, or completed one-time actions like a login prompt.

rule: Persist user-locked windows and volumes in their original rooms to create a sense of presence and continuity in spatial interfaces.
quote: visionOS 26 brings over some macOS lifecycle APIs that will come in quite handy. We'll cover APIs to manage scene restoration and app launch as well as an API to create unique windows. In visionOS 26, people can now persist windows, volumes, and even the new widgets by locking them to particular rooms in their physical surroundings.

rule: Make animation playback controllable and observable in SwiftUI to allow users to pause, resume, and scrub through 3D model animations.
quote: The asset vends an `animationPlaybackController`. Use this object to pause, resume, and seek in the animation.

rule: Avoid menus as primary navigation; provide context and clear structure first.
quote: Menus can be vague and unpredictable, and what I really need first is some context.

rule: Organize information by removing non-essential features, clarifying naming, and grouping related items.
quote: I start cleaning things up — removing features that aren't essential, renaming things that aren't clear, and grouping those that naturally belong together.

rule: Use tab bar navigation to help people access main features; limit tabs to essential items only.
quote: Simplifying it matters because each extra tab means one more decision for people to make and might present the app as much more complex that what it really is.

rule: Use rounded shapes for interactive elements; they draw eyes to the center and feel more inviting.
quote: For interactive elements, prefer rounded shapes, like circles, pills, and rounded rectangles, they're easier to look at, drawing your eyes to the center of the shape.

rule: Give interactive elements at least 60 points of touch or eye-tracking target space.
quote: For precise interactions, give each element at least 60 points of space. Elements can be visually smaller than this, as long they each have a total space of 60 points.

rule: Apply highlight effects to all interactive elements to signal they are selectable.
quote: Apply highlight effects to all interactive elements. Standard components like this menu will highlight automatically.

rule: Use ramp animations (slow ease-in then quick spring) when views expand to show more content.
quote: To create your own ramp animation, try a curve like this. It starts with a slow ease-in, then pops to completion with a quick spring. This animation curve tends to work best when views expand to show more content.

rule: Make navigation adaptive; resize without destroying layout, reverting when possible.
quote: When adapting to size changes, make sure that any change in layout is non-destructive. Resizing an app should not permanently alter its layout. Be opportunistic about reverting back to the starting state whenever possible.

rule: Extend content around navigation controls using scroll edge effect and content below sidebars.
quote: People come to your app for its content. So use as much of the display as possible to create the most immersive experience. You can start doing this by drawing content below the toolbar using the new 'scroll edge effect'.

rule: Spatial video renders with windowed treatment by default; expand immersively to scale content to real size.
quote: By default, spatial video renders through a window, with a faint glow around the edges. It can also expand into an immersive presentation, where the content is scaled to match the real size of objects.

rule: Use larger text in snippets to draw attention to important information; text is larger than system defaults.
quote: A key aspect to making the snippet glanceable is type size. Text in snippets are larger than system defaults. Larger type draws attention to the most important information in the moment.

rule: Keep snippet height under 340 points to avoid scrolling; link to app for additional information.
quote: Avoid including content past 340 points in height, which will require scrolling and introduce unexpected friction. Instead, keep the content concise with only the most important information.

rule: Use vibrant backgrounds but check contrast beyond standard ratios; increase contrast for distant viewing.
quote: It's especially important to check for contrast when the snippet is viewed from a distance, going beyond standard contrast ratios. If the content is hard to read, try increasing the contrast between the content in the layout and the background.

rule: Update data within snippet after button action to confirm success and build trust.
quote: By updating the data within the snippet itself to confirm that the action was successful, people can build trust in your App Intent for their routines.

rule: Use consistent, real-world scale for widgets to feel well-proportioned in any placement.
quote: Widgets have a consistent, real-world scale, helping them to feel well-proportioned wherever they are placed.

rule: Adapt widget appearance and layout based on viewing distance to show appropriate detail levels.
quote: Widgets on visionOS adapt their appearance and layout based on how close someone is, always showing the right level of detail

rule: Design widgets for glanceable legibility from across the room when wall-mounted.
quote: The text size is designed to be glanceable from across the room, ensuring legibility when wall-mounted.

rule: Use lensing to provide visual separation and communicate layering while letting content show through.
quote: Liquid Glass uses these instinctive visual cues to provide separation and communicate layering in a new way while letting content shine through underneath it.

rule: Transition elements by gradually modulating light bending instead of fading for optical integrity.
quote: Instead of fading, Liquid Glass objects materialize in and out by gradually modulating the light bending and lensing, ensuring a graceful transition

rule: Calculate depth and Z position for 3D views alongside width, height, and XY position in layout systems.
quote: for each of your views, in addition to width and height, SwiftUI also calculates a depth and a Z position.

rule: Use scaledToFit3D modifier to maintain model aspect ratio while scaling across all three dimensions.
quote: scaledToFit3D modifier in addition to resizable(), causing my robot to maintain the model's aspect ratio while still sizing up or down to fit the available width, height, and now depth.

rule: Allow tab bars to minimize on scroll to keep focus on content rather than chrome.
quote: With the new design, the tab bar on iPhone floats above the content, and can be configured to minimize on scroll, keeping the focus on your content.

rule: Adjust accessory view visibility when inline with tab bar due to reduced space availability.
quote: When the accessory is inline with the tab bar, there is less space available to display it. Here, the Music app is accommodating the reduced space by hiding some of the media controls

rule: Design symbol paths with draw direction intention: left-to-right for motion, right-to-left for Arabic, center for symmetry.
quote: We've designed Draw to be flexible, allowing each symbol to define how it is drawn. For example, wind draws left to right to convey motion, whereas this Arabic character draws from right to left

rule: Use Variable Draw to render path progress as a percentage with reduced opacity background layer.
quote: Variable draw leverages the new draw annotations on participating layers. It renders the path at a specific percentage on top of a reduced opacity version of the layer.

rule: Make Liquid Glass adapt automatically to underlying content darkness, changing from light to dark on scroll.
quote: As you scroll through content, the glass automatically adapts to the content underneath, changing from light to dark.

rule: Use backgroundExtensionEffect to extend content outside safe area without clipping when behind overlays.
quote: With the new backgroundExtensionEffect modifier, views can extend outside the safe area, without clipping their content.

rule: Configure tab bar to minimize on scroll to prioritize content visibility over navigation chrome.
quote: With the new design, the tab bar on iPhone floats above the content, and can be configured to minimize on scroll. This lets your app's content remain the star of the show.

rule: Account for all watch display dimensions when designing layouts; ensure apps deliver same information and actions across all screen sizes.
quote: Your app should deliver the same information and actions to the user, regardless of screen size.

rule: Extend graphic elements and button backgrounds nearly edge-to-edge, respecting one-pixel margins on watch displays.
quote: Graphic elements and button backgrounds should extend beyond these margins and run nearly edge to edge, up to the one pixel margin that runs by default on either side.

rule: Use scroll clear areas at top and bottom to ensure text and buttons are fully visible when users complete scrolling actions on watches.
quote: To account for the corners in scroll views, there are clear areas at the top and bottom of the content area. These are known as scroll clear areas, and they ensure that text and buttons are nudged fully into view when the user completes a scrolling action.

rule: Recompile apps for watchOS 5 to allow full use of new Series 4 display dimensions and create immersive experiences.
quote: Recompiling your app for watchOS 5 will allow your app to occupy the full width and height of the new display. As long as you've implemented your WatchKit elements relative to their containers rather than at fixed widths, your app will expand to fill the additional screen space on Series 4 watches, and this will feel much more immersive and engaging to your users.

rule: Present subscription offers at moments when users show interest in gated features or content.
quote: Another way to be visible would be to present your subscription when a person has shown interest in a feature or piece of content that you offer through your subscription.

rule: Minimize clicks in subscription flows; three clicks achieves 61% conversion, nine clicks drops to 7%.
quote: A subscription flow with three clicks led to a 61 percent conversion rate, and a subscription flow with four clicks led to a 48 percent conversion rate. However, nine clicks... the conversation rate drops significantly to seven percent.
finding: 3 clicks = 61% conversion, 4 clicks = 48%, 9 clicks = 7%

rule: Ask for signup before requesting personalization, favoriting, or additional personal details in subscription flows.
quote: Focus people on singing up first. Personalization, favoriting, and requesting additional personal details can all wait until after someone has signed up.

rule: Make subscription offers glanceable; include value proposition, call to action, login option, restore purchase, clear terms, pricing, and multiple tiers in one view.
quote: Strive to be glanceable; in one view and in just a few seconds, people should be able to clearly understand what your subscription offer is and how to sign up.

rule: Use PDFs for image assets on high-density displays to reduce app size and ensure resolution independence.
quote: When producing and delivering image assets, we recommend using PDFs because they're resolution-independent and may significantly reduce the size of your app.

rule: Use layout margins to provide consistent content margins across apps and align content with controls like navigation bar buttons.
quote: Layout margins provide consistent content margins across apps and help you to align content to other controls like navigation bar buttons.

rule: Fill the entire display with app content; avoid placing black bars at top or bottom as this makes apps feel small and inconsistent.
quote: Your app or game should always fill the display that it runs on. Placing black bars at the top or bottom of the screen makes your app feel small, cramped, and inconsistent with other apps on iPhone X.

rule: Consider different aspect ratios when designing background graphics for devices with varying screen proportions.
quote: When designing background graphics, or rendering background scenes, keep in mind that iPhone X's display has a different aspect ratio than a 4.7 inch display.

rule: Break down complex reasoning tasks into simpler steps when using smaller on-device language models.
quote: If you're not getting good results with a system model for a complex reasoning task, try breaking down your task prompt into simpler steps.

rule: Avoid using on-device language models for calculations; use non-AI code instead for math-related tasks.
quote: For math-related tasks, you're gonna wanna avoid asking this small model to act as a calculator. Non-AI code is much more reliable for math.

rule: Provide verified information in prompts when generating facts; thoroughly fact-check model outputs for new prompts.
quote: If you do want to generate facts, consider providing the model with verified information written into your prompt. And thoroughly fact check model outputs for any new prompts you write.

rule: Use guided generation to control what the model generates, whether strings, numbers, arrays, or custom data structures.
quote: With the Foundation Models Framework, Guided generation gives you control over what the model should generate, whether that be strings, numbers, arrays, or a custom data structure that you define.

rule: Present momentary information like alerts, sheets, menus, and popovers inside and on top of volumes so they break through content and remain visible.
quote: Momentary information like alerts, sheets, menus, and popovers are frequently used in apps and are an essential part of its user experience. In visionOS 26, presenting this transient content inside and on top of volumes becomes possible. In spatial experiences where 3D content can overlap user interfaces, key elements like presentations will break through the content to remain visible.

rule: Configure dynamic bounds restrictions to allow app content to peek outside its bounds and blend seamlessly with the real world.
quote: Now by configuring dynamic bounds restrictions, your apps can blend even more seamlessly with the real world by rendering outside your app's bounds. You can apply this effect to your apps by adding a simple view modifier, specifying how much you want your content to peek outside its bounds.

rule: Allow objects to rotate intuitively with the user's hand as if they were holding the real thing to create natural interaction.
quote: Interacting with virtual objects should feel natural, mimicking the real world. Now, objects can rotate intuitively with the user's hand as if they were holding the real thing.

rule: Remove unnecessary adverbs and adjectives from UI copy; they often function as fillers without adding clarity.
quote: Adverbs are words that describe actions like "easily" and "quickly". And adjectives describe nouns. Those include words like "fast" and "simple". Of course, there are many more, and when you notice words like these, it's worth a pause to see if they're needed.

rule: Remove interjections and pleasantries like "oops," "sorry," and "thank you" from error messages and alerts unless they add meaning.
quote: Interjections are abrupt words or phrases like "oops," "oh no," and "hooray." These are remarks used in polite conversation like "sorry," "thank you," and "please." While it might seem like these words make your app feel more personal, it's best to remove them when they don't add any meaning to the message.

rule: Avoid phrases like "uh oh" and "oh no" in error messages; they undermine the seriousness of the problem.
quote: Words like "uh oh, "oops" or "oh no!" in error messages can make it sound like you're not taking the problem seriously.

rule: Lead with the benefit or purpose of an action to give sentences more impact and clarity.
quote: Later, Jen will show you how to lead with the why by doing some hands-on editing to give your sentences more impact.

rule: Create and maintain a word list to ensure consistency across your app's writing.
quote: And she'll conclude by talking about how a word list makes it easy to keep consistency in your app.

rule: Define your app's voice through consistent qualities like clarity, simplicity, friendliness, and helpfulness that guide all writing.
quote: Clarity, simplicity, friendliness, and helpfulness. Your voice will be different, but I see these pretty consistently throughout Apple's writing

rule: Use exclamation points sparingly, reserving them for genuinely celebratory or urgent moments to maintain impact.
quote: we tend to use exclamation marks pretty sparingly around here, this screen gets one, because of the situation

rule: Test visual effects over time and in different contexts to confirm they remain pleasant after novelty wears off.
quote: Visual effects should be pleasant to use well after the novelty has worn off. Testing your effects over time, and in different contexts will help reinforce if an effect is working

rule: Use scroll transitions to change rotation, offset, or opacity based on element position, creating unique scroll experiences.
quote: Scroll transition exposes the content I'd like to transition, as well as a phase. I can use these values to change the rotation, and offset of each photo

rule: Anchor primary interactions to the Digital Crown, with touch as a backup, to match the watch's input paradigm.
quote: In watchOS 10, we are emphasizing the Digital Crown as the way you get to and navigate through apps, to scroll, paginate, and make precise adjustments. While interactions should be anchored to the crown, they should also always be backed up by touch.

rule: Test interactions on the actual device to accurately validate how layouts, animations, and gestures feel in real use.
quote: we developed all our designs in SwiftUI, right on device. This gave us control over every detail, from spacing and typestyles to animations and interactions.

rule: Position tab bars at the top of the app, closer to navigation controls, to make them easier to reach.
quote: The bar now sits at the top of the app, where it is closer to other navigation controls, making it easier to reach.

rule: Limit the number of tabs to avoid making it harder for people to locate information within your app.
quote: Avoid adding too many tabs. Too many choices make it harder for people to locate information within your app.

rule: Use outline glyph variants for tab symbols; the system automatically selects the filled variant in tab bars.
quote: Tab bars prefer filled glyphs, and sidebars prefer outlined glyphs. When using symbol images for your tabs, use the outline variant. The system will automatically select the filled variant when displayed in the tab bar.

rule: Keep tab state consistent between iPhone and iPad so people can navigate easily regardless of device.
quote: Tabs should be consistent between iPhone and iPad to allow people to navigate easily no matter what device they are using.

rule: Enable multiview layout templates that maximize comfort and ergonomics when displaying multiple simultaneous video screens.
quote: Multiview allows up to five video screens at once, with layout templates that maximize comfort and viewability.

rule: Designate one video as main-focus to receive direct playback controls and audio priority in multiview experiences.
quote: The original video has main focus, which includes a slightly more prominent look and audio playback. When I close the content browser, I get the familiar media playback controls and the main-focus video responds directly to these controls.

rule: Use photorealistic assets with high visual quality to make spatial content feel convincing and compelling.
quote: As a baseline, assets need to be photorealistic with a high degree of visual quality to feel convincing and compelling.

rule: Bring spatial content to life through animations that replicate real scenarios or enable manipulation not easily done in reality.
quote: To make new things possible, bring your content to life. Consider how animations can replicate real scenarios, like you see here with air simulation in the intake fan. Or provide ways to manipulate models that would be cumbersome in the real world.

rule: Make zoom transitions continuously interactive, allowing users to grab and drag the element during the transition.
quote: With this new transition, the cell you tap morphs into the incoming view. And it's not just a new visual appearance, it also is continuously interactive, allowing you to grab and drag it around, from the beginning or during the transition.

rule: Bundle the first 15 minutes of gameplay into the initial app download to let players start immediately upon installation.
quote: Aim to get around the first 15 minutes of gameplay bundled into your App Store download.

rule: Hide background downloads from players; load additional game data behind the scenes after installation.
quote: Try to hide download progress from players. In many cases they'll never have to know that data is still loading in, and it will feel like your whole game was playable at launch.

rule: Set sensible defaults automatically based on device hardware to reduce onboarding choices for players.
quote: You can simplify your game's onboarding by setting options automatically for players. For example, in your onboarding and settings, look for places to remove choices that aren't relevant. Like asking for screen size or aspect ratio, which you just get from the device itself.

rule: Automatically detect paired controllers and map buttons to UI without requiring manual player setup.
quote: Instead of having folks manually set up a physical game controller, you can automatically detect whether a controller is paired and get its profile by using the Game Controller Framework.

rule: Adjust initial performance settings to match device capabilities across different platforms.
quote: When choosing defaults across different platforms, consider adjusting your game's initial performance settings to match the capabilities of that device. For example, you might choose to set quality defaults higher, for a top-of-the-line Mac, than you would for an iPhone.

rule: Reduce settings granularity on mobile platforms to prioritize quick startup and simplified choices.
quote: Especially on mobile platforms, remember that players just want to pick up their device and go. So look for opportunities where you can reduce the granularity of your settings, compared to what you might offer on a desktop.

rule: Make Live Activities on Apple Watch highly glanceable, showing only the most critical information needed.
quote: Live Activities on Apple Watch are meant to be highly glanceable, providing just the information you need, and nothing more.

rule: Display a compact Live Activity view at the bottom of the screen when updates occur while users are in another app.
quote: To ensure people never miss an update from your Live Activity we've created the compact view When you're interacting with an app and a Live Activity receives an update, like the status of your food delivery changing, a smaller, more compact version of the Live Activity appears at the bottom of the display.

rule: Auto-present the Smart Stack when a Live Activity starts so users can see status by raising their wrist.
quote: On Apple Watch, when a Live Activity starts, the Smart Stack is automatically presented and displays a widget for that Live Activity. This allows you to see the status of a Live Activity just by raising your wrist, without having to first rotate the Digital Crown.

rule: Let players make small hand movements that amplify into big actions; use indirect input for comfortable longer play sessions.
quote: Indirect input lets players make small hand movements that are amplified into big actions.

rule: For direct input interactions, include abundant visual and audio feedback so every contact feels satisfying.
quote: If this type of input fits your game, make sure to include plenty of feedback, so every contact with an object feels satisfying for the player.

rule: Prefer system gestures; players already know them and need no extra equipment or learning.
quote: For one thing, players already know exactly how to use the system gestures, because they're already using them to navigate all the other apps and games on the platform.

rule: Use Wiggle animation to highlight changes or call-to-action elements that might be overlooked.
quote: You can use the Wiggle preset when you want to highlight changes or a call to action that might be overlooked.

rule: Use Breathe animation to convey status changes or signal that an activity is taking place with more lifelike presence.
quote: Breathe is the animation that smoothly increases and decreases the presence of a symbol, giving it a living quality.

rule: Use Rotate animation to indicate progress or imitate real-world object behavior as a visual indicator.
quote: With Rotate you can add dynamic movement to a symbol by imitating how an object behaves in the real world, or by acting as a visual indicator.

rule: Simplify 3D geometry to only the complexity necessary to communicate assets with enough detail; decimate distant assets.
quote: Geometry should be as complex as necessary to communicate the asset with enough detail.

rule: Use texture baking to combine all surface characteristics into single images, reducing total textures and computational load.
quote: Texture Baking, which captures all surface characteristics of 3D objects into a single image. This image can then be reapplied to the objects, making them look realistic and detailed without additional raytracing.

rule: Test lighting perception on both monitor and headset, as they differ; offer multiple lighting modes for viewer choice.
quote: As you test the lighting, it is important to note that how you perceive light varies between monitor and headset.

rule: Design for variable environments; what works indoors in a living room may not work outdoors in a park.
quote: What works indoors in someone's living room might not work outdoors in a park.

rule: Surface all app functionality as app intents, not just habitual tasks; balance flexibility with clarity to avoid brittle intents.
quote: Now, anything your app does should be an app intent.

rule: Do not create app intents that exclusively trigger specific UI elements; intents should represent underlying tasks.
quote: App intents should not exclusively trigger specific UI elements, such as tapping a cancel button, or swiping down on a platter.

rule: Ensure parameter summaries remain readable as sentences regardless of which option is selected.
quote: Since the parameter can be changed to any of these camera modes, it's important to make sure the summary is always readable as a sentence, regardless of which mode you select.

rule: Use hover effects to provide feedback about which element will trigger when users tap their fingers together.
quote: Hover effects make your app feel responsive while providing feedback about which element will be triggered when people tap their fingers together.

rule: Respect accessibility preferences when building custom hover effects; ensure effects are comfortable and preserve privacy.
quote: Custom hover effects were designed from the ground up to preserve privacy. They're applied by the system, outside the app process.

rule: Place main content in the center of the field of view; reserve edges for secondary actions only.
quote: Try to keep the main content of the app in the center of the field of view, the most comfortable area for your eyes.

rule: Keep all interactive content at the same depth to avoid eye strain from refocusing.
quote: Look to keep interactive content at the same depth to make it feel effortless to switch between UI.

rule: Use round shapes and avoid sharp edges to guide eye focus to element centers.
quote: Use round shapes like circles, pills, and rounded rectangles. Avoid using shapes with sharp edges.

rule: Target tips only to users who would benefit; use eligibility rules to avoid reaching uninterested or already-informed audiences.
quote: In-app education should be focused on those who would benefit from it, and we aim to avoid getting in the way of individuals while they are trying to accomplish something in an app.

rule: Design shortcuts to perform direct actions, not mirror tab-bar navigation or secondary workflows.
quote: Prefer shortcuts that take action directly. Your first idea might be to look at your app's tab bar and reflect it directly into shortcuts, but challenge yourself to think of something better.

rule: Order shortcuts to match the user's mental model and decisions made inside the app to build muscle memory.
quote: You should order your shortcuts to reflect the decisions people make inside your app, and to help people build muscle memory around things being in predictable places.

rule: Vary pitch and amplitude of repetitive interaction sounds to feel more natural than static repetition.
quote: when you know a sound will be played often, it helps to slightly randomize some elements of the sound like its pitch and amplitude

rule: Use spatial audio to place interaction sounds at their visual locations on screen for natural feedback.
quote: the sound of each key press and how it comes from its location on the keyboard in front of you. Each time you interact with the keys, the familiar sound confirms your action

rule: Animate symbols by layer separately to create clear, precise choreography that guides visual hierarchy.
quote: By default, a symbol will animate by layer. This means that each layer will animate one at a time, making the symbol's choreography have clear and precise movements

rule: Annotate custom symbols to specify which layers should animate when using layer-by-layer animation presets.
quote: a new control in the annotation list here that allows you to specify which layers should pulse when you're using the By Layer setting

rule: Make background content supporting, not decorative; it should provide utility aligned with the app's function.
quote: Background content in watchOS 10 should play a supporting role that provides additional utility, not merely be a visual flourish

rule: Use translucent materials to establish hierarchy and help users understand navigation context within the system.
quote: Distinct, functional layers utilize translucency to establish hierarchy and help users understand where they are in the system or inside an app

rule: Choose features for shortcuts that are self-contained and can be completed outside the app without opening it.
quote: A great App Shortcut is one that actually doesn't require your app in focus at all. You're looking for a lightweight task that can be completed via Siri or via search in its entirety.

rule: Name app shortcuts with brief, memorable phrases that clearly communicate function and include the app name naturally.
quote: The first important thing to remember when you're crafting that hero phrase is to keep it brief. You want your app shortcut phrase to be easy to remember and to clearly communicate its function.

rule: Use Palette rendering mode with two or more contrasting colors to give symbol elements prominence and allow customization to environment color palettes.
quote: Palette uses two or more contrasting colors to give elements of a symbol more prominence and versatility, allowing for the symbols to be customized to integrate with the color palette of the environment.

rule: Prioritize information visibility by sizing and scaling elements to be visible at a quick glance.
quote: Think about the information you would find most useful and prioritize the sizing and scale of those elements to be visible at a quick glance.

rule: Maintain visual connection between Live Activity and app by sharing colors, iconography, and typeface.
quote: As you design your graphical layout, consider the colors, iconography, typefaces, and other attributes from your app that you can use. The goal and best end result is when your Live Activity and app feel like they share the same visual aesthetic and personality.

rule: Preserve color associations between Light and Dark modes to maintain visual connection with app icon.
quote: Don't alter your colors between light and dark mode if it breaks this visual association.

rule: Integrate logo marks into layout structure rather than displaying the full app icon.
quote: If you do use a logo mark as part of your brand, make sure it's integrated uncontained into the layout itself rather than just using your whole app icon.

rule: Dynamically adjust Live Activity height based on available information to reduce clutter.
quote: Another way to use space efficiently is to dynamically change the height of your Live Activity between different moments as you have more or less information to display.

rule: Ensure all depth cues in 3D content align to give the brain correct depth information.
quote: Ensure all of the depth cues from your content give the brain correct information so to align the viewer's eyes to the depth you intended.

rule: Add missing depth cues using color, blur, relative size, motion, background, light, shadow, occlusion, and texture.
quote: An added background, light and shadow, occlusion, and texture density are some more methods to add in the missing visual depth cues.

rule: Place content requiring extended fixation farther than arm's-length distance for visual comfort.
quote: Content requiring fixating the eyes for an extended time, such as for reading, is most visually comfortable when placed farther than arm's-length distance.

rule: Enable users to adjust content depth to choose a comfortable distance for their viewing.
quote: In addition, enable a person to adjust content depth so they may choose a depth that's most comfortable for them in the experience.

rule: Present windowed shared activities to support multitasking and collaboration without leaving surroundings.
quote: Putting your activity in a window is a great way to support multitasking and collaboration and doesn't require people to leave their surroundings.

rule: Minimize setup steps when joining shared activities; start activity for permitted users and show placeholders for others.
quote: Minimize the amount of setup involved in joining. If your shared activity does need additional steps to get started, start the activity for people who have the right permissions and present a placeholder window to those who don't.

rule: Avoid launching extra windows unrelated to the shared activity.
quote: When possible, don't launch any extra windows unrelated to the shared activity.

rule: Keep app icon graphics centered to avoid appearing off-center when expanded.
quote: Try to keep graphics centered. If they are too close to the edge, they could look off-center when expanded.

rule: Avoid large semitransparent regions in app icon layers to prevent blending with shadows.
quote: Avoid using large regions of semitransparent pixels. Layers with reduced opacity will blend with the shadow cast behind it.

rule: Avoid stacking multiple lighter materials to maintain legibility and contrast.
quote: Try to not stack lighter materials on top of each other, as it impacts legibility and reduces contrast.

rule: Use width styles—Condensed, Compressed, or Expanded—to accommodate space constraints and stylistic needs in UI design.
quote: adding a Width axis was the natural evolution of SF: Joining the Regular Width we have three more styles: Condensed, narrow and space-efficient; Compressed, the most compact style currently available in SF; and last but not least, on the other end of the spectrum, Expanded.

rule: Match font weight and width choices to typographic hierarchy intent: neutral styles for balance, extreme proportions for emphasis and attention.
quote: you can expect the styles that gravitate towards the center of the stylistic map of SF to have a more neutral voice, while the styles around the perimeter of the map, which feature more extreme Weight and Width proportions, to be more expressive, have a stronger voice, attributes that can be useful if you want to draw people's attention towards a certain area of the UI or strengthen a typographic hierarchy.

rule: Display button glyphs that match the specific controller type the player is holding, so UI looks correct across different controller families.
quote: Consider this hint to use a button to display your inventory. On an MFi or Xbox controller, we should show the Y button. On a PlayStation controller, we instead want to show a triangle.

rule: Abstract input hardware through a common API to write input code once without worrying about controller remapping or hardware differences.
quote: By abstracting input hardware through the common API, the game controller framework lets you write your input code once without having to worry about how input may have been remapped or the differences among specific controllers, keyboards, or pointing devices.

rule: Use optical margins in symbol templates to ensure symbols align correctly with one another when displayed in lists and table views.
quote: margins for making sure symbols are optically centered with one another when used in lists and table views

rule: Design symbols with multiple weights to match text styling and adapt to features such as accessibility bold on iOS.
quote: Multiple weights to match text and adjust to features such as accessibility bold on iOS

rule: Provide three weight-matched scales in custom symbols to adjust symbol appearance across different UI contexts and element sizes.
quote: three weight-matched scales to adjust to the context of different UI elements

rule: Order screen information by importance; place the most critical message at the top.
quote: think about the most important thing someone needs to know at that moment. That's the purpose of your screen.

rule: Make headers and buttons clear because people do not read screens linearly.
quote: people don't always read the text on screen in order, so make sure your headers and buttons are clear.

rule: Use familiar navigation patterns so users focus on content rather than learning how to navigate.
quote: Familiar navigation patterns can help people easily explore the information within your app — and save them from unnecessary confusion.

rule: Organize app functionality into balanced, focused sections rather than cramming features into one tab.
quote: It's much easier to understand an app's functionality when it's well organized and clearly communicated.

rule: Distribute functionality evenly across tabs instead of loading the first tab heavily.
quote: Try to create balance in your interface by distributing functionality throughout your tabs.

rule: Use the system share sheet to help users begin collaboration in a familiar, consistent way.
quote: The system share sheet gives people an easy way to begin a collaboration. It will help make collaboration in your app more consistent and familiar.

rule: Place the share button in toolbars where people can easily access it.
quote: Put the button in a place where people can easily access. Toolbars are a good candidate.

rule: Write concise copy for permission settings to avoid truncation and aid quick decision-making.
quote: You need to provide a descriptive copy of default settings your app supports. To avoid truncation, be as concise as possible.

rule: Keep permission settings screens simple so users can easily skim options and decide quickly.
quote: keep the structure of choices simple so people can easily skim the options and make quick decisions.

rule: Design SharePlay activities to bring people together through shared experiences beyond text or video alone.
quote: some of the most meaningful moments people have together are about more than just sharing a conversation. When we're together, we connect most by sharing experiences.

rule: For Arabic layouts, reverse entire layout directionality so content flows from right to left to match reading behavior.
quote: If this phrase exists in a layout, the entire layout flows from top to bottom, right to left, to match the reading behavior and direction of the language.

rule: Invert carousel and animation interactions in right-to-left layouts to match the inverted UI direction.
quote: Both, the interaction and the animation of this component are inverted to match the UI direction.

rule: For Arabic layouts, reverse entire layout directionality so content flows from right to left to match reading behavior.
quote: If this phrase exists in a layout, the entire layout flows from top to bottom, right to left, to match the reading behavior and direction of the language.

rule: Invert carousel and animation interactions in right-to-left layouts to match the inverted UI direction.
quote: Both, the interaction and the animation of this component are inverted to match the UI direction.

rule: Accompany every chart with text describing its contents; if isolated, the description should be informative.
quote: A chart should be accompanied by text that describes the chart contents. If read in isolation, it should be informative.

rule: Use charts to direct attention to the most important information, not to visualize everything possible.
quote: Charts are a strong signal. They direct attention to the information you want them to understand.

rule: Design charts with focused intent on a few key insights, not every possible insight in the data.
quote: An effective chart focuses on a few key pieces of information. Design charts with intention.

rule: Round percentage thresholds to whole numbers to avoid rounding errors in symbol appearance.
quote: Thresholds between layers are rounded to the nearest percentage point, and we don't activate the next layer until you're one full percentage point above that rounded value.

rule: Involve physical space meaningfully in AR experiences so they respond to and affect the user's immediate surroundings.
quote: AR is at its most delightful when it affects and responds to what's immediately around you, involving physical space in a meaningful way.

rule: Use AR to enable people to visualize and try on objects in 3D before making decisions or purchases.
quote: With AR, you can build features that help people try on things in a way that's virtual yet realistic enough for someone to make a confident purchasing decision.

rule: Keep AR experiences lightweight with minimal UI when the interaction is device movement and information is temporary.
quote: The experience feels lightweight because there's very little UI, the interaction is based on device movement, and the measurement information disappears after you've seen it.

rule: Show diverse people and activities in app screenshots and marketing to help users from different backgrounds feel included.
quote: The way you describe your app or game, its name, video trailer, and even the screenshots you select tell a story about whom it was built for

rule: Use inclusive language and imagery that reflects diverse backgrounds, cultures, languages, and abilities throughout your interface and content.
quote: An inclusive app or game is not only usable by different people, but also welcomes people from diverse backgrounds and perspectives.

rule: Let people customize names, avatars, and profile details to represent themselves authentically in your app.
quote: It's also how you let folks identify themselves. This can be through the names, profile details, avatars, or characters that people can customize

rule: Ensure haptic feedback clearly corresponds to its visual cause so users understand what triggered the sensation.
quote: For feedback to be useful, it must be obvious what caused it. It's about making the source or the cause of the feedback clear and obvious.

rule: Reserve haptics and audio feedback for significant moments and actions; avoid overusing them or they become overwhelming.
quote: Don't add feedback just because you can. It can quickly become overwhelming and unpleasant. Reserve haptics and audio for significant moments

rule: Make App Clips lightweight by including only essential functionality needed for the immediate task.
quote: App Clips are lightweight versions of apps. They offer some of an app's functionality and they offer it when and where people need it.

rule: Use menus instead of action sheets on iPad and large screens to avoid heavy background dimming and better preserve context.
quote: Upon appearing, they dimmed the background, which causes a heavy transition, especially on larger screens like an iPad.

rule: Position menus near where users tap to minimize finger movement and improve speed of selection.
quote: To start, the menu appears right next to where you tapped, and that requires far less movement of your finger to select an action.

rule: Use menus to organize secondary or less critical actions and reduce visual clutter in your interface.
quote: A simple more button in a view is a great way to show a menu of actions. These actions are often not important enough to be prominently displayed

rule: Provide the right value at the right time to help users accomplish their goals and develop lasting habits with your app.
quote: Learn how you can provide the right kind of value at the right time to help them in their everyday tasks

rule: Place the Game Center access point on your game's main menu where possible.
quote: Whenever possible, display your access point at your game's main menu.

rule: Position the access point in the top left corner of the screen if feasible.
quote: However, we'd recommend placing it at top left, if possible.

rule: Reserve safe areas around the access point to prevent game UI overlap.
quote: You'll just want to make sure none of your game's UI encroaches upon the area the access point takes at its maximum size.
finding: iPhone 11 Pro portrait: 62×335 points with 114-point safe area; landscape: 62×280 points with 91-point safe area

rule: Never rely on color alone to convey meaning; add shapes or icons.
quote: using color only to create emphasis can get lost. There are extra steps you can take to achieve good design, and I'll give you a hint: It's shapes.

rule: Provide alternate button appearance when button shapes accessibility setting is enabled.
quote: If you can't fit button shapes in your default design, you should provide an alternate appearance for people with this setting enabled.

rule: Define key repeatable actions in your app using the Intents framework.
quote: Ultimately, you, as developers and designers, just need to ask yourself, what are the important actions that people want to perform with your app?

rule: Ensure Siri dialogue sounds natural with your app's actual data.
quote: you should still make sure that the dialogue sounds good with your data in it, both from a sentence structure perspective and a text-to-speech perspective.

rule: Use adaptive precision to adjust pointer behavior to match interface element size.
quote: dynamically adjusting the precision of the pointer to match the precision of the interface is called, Adaptive Precision.

rule: Ensure the pointer highlights controls without obscuring them.
quote: the pointer highlights the element rather than obscuring it.

rule: Group navigation items logically to reduce wait time for Switch Control users.
quote: the efficiency and grouping of these navigation items is key for Switch Control users, as poor grouping can lead to large wait times to arrive at the item of interest.

rule: Make destructive actions error-tolerant for users with limited motor control.
quote: If there's an option to delete all data or log out, one accidental tap could have quite destructive consequences for a Switch Control user, so error tolerance is very important.

rule: Start accessibility work by understanding a product's core mission and primary use case.
quote: What is the product supposed to do? What is its core mission of what this is gonna bring value for?

rule: Measure and test motion sensitivity in apps and games; provide reduced-motion modes for users with motion sensitivities.
quote: Turning on reduced motion in a game so people with motion sensitivities can still have fun and experience the game fully.

rule: Present accessibility controls and warnings upfront so users discover them before encountering barriers.
quote: This app has got some really great visual warnings about potential sensory and cognitive needs. It's also very good at presenting those controls and those warnings upfront.

rule: Remove layers of abstraction by letting users interact directly with physical surroundings via device proximity.
quote: These human-scale interactions -- the ones that happen between devices nearby -- have the ability to remove layers of abstraction and allow users to interact more directly with their surroundings.

rule: Identify activities in your app that people naturally want to do together; design for group-first sharing.
quote: All these examples are things people love to do together. You should look for activities in your app to bring people together, encourage conversation, collaboration, or just enjoyment.

rule: Restrict visibility of sensitive data during screen sharing by default; exclude secure entry fields automatically.
quote: By default, everything is shared except for secure entry fields. You can use UIKit API to further restrict the visibility of this information on iOS during screen sharing sessions.

rule: View your app through multiple axes of diversity including ability, language, culture, class, and connectivity.
quote: Diversity axes can include class; culture; ethnicity; language; education; political, philosophical and religious beliefs; race; gender; sexual orientation; age; abilities; disabilities; whether you are right- or left-handed; body measurements like height; and also environmental conditions like location, internet connectivity, or access to technology devices.

rule: Empower diverse teams to voice ideas; accessible solutions often emerge from diverse perspectives.
quote: In truth, having an empowered diverse team means your app or game can be inclusive. We all share the responsibility to build an inclusive environment that enables inclusive actions.

rule: Use constraints as tools to narrow the problem space and drive creative solutions.
quote: Constraints help your process by helping you make the first few early decisions. This allows you to put most of your energy into creating new solutions in a narrow problem space.

rule: Use system symbols that automatically localize for different languages and text directions.
quote: The symbol I grabbed for my rule book earlier automatically appears with a character in the user's native script. It even adjusts the direction that the book opens to account for differences between left-to-right and right-to-left languages.

rule: Check platform and OS version compatibility of symbols before using them in shipped code.
quote: The information inspector that the name person.fill.badge.plus has been available in monochrome since SF Symbols version 2.0, which corresponds to iOS 14; that's too new for me.

rule: Use Label views to pair icons with text, as they adapt their layout to context automatically.
quote: A Label is a combination of a title with an icon, which is most often a symbol. The great thing about a label is that it's a general description of this pairing and will adapt its behavior to the context where it's shown.

rule: Localize custom symbol names in Localizable.strings files so SwiftUI uses them automatically for accessibility.
quote: A great way to improve that is to provide a localization for the image's name in a Localizable.strings file. SwiftUI will automatically use this localizable string for the accessibility label of this image anywhere it's used.

rule: Use text styles like body or caption with symbols so both text and symbols scale with dynamic type.
quote: If you use a text style, like body or caption, then the text and symbol will scale with dynamic type, and if you choose a fixed size, then they stay constant.
