quote: rather than keeping the count inline, I can use a badge on the inbox to turn an item that displays both text and a symbol into a symbol-only item

rule: Prioritize which items stay visible longest in overflow: use visibilityPriority(high) for frequently-used actions and status indicators.
quote: Frequently used actions like Compose in Mail or New Note in Notes should be amongst the last to move into overflow. Likewise, controls that convey important status, such as items with badges, should remain visible for longer

rule: Persist tab customizations automatically so users do not lose their organized layout.
quote: Customizations to the order and visibility are automatically persisted.

rule: Designate fixed tabs for essential app destinations to prevent users from hiding them.
quote: The fixed section is designed for important destinations of your app. They appear before other items and disallow customization.

rule: Place search functionality in the pinned trailing section of tab bars for consistent access.
quote: Items in the pinned section, like search, are always available in the trailing edge of the tab bar.

rule: Start with single-view playback and suggest multiview only when users explicitly opt in.
quote: Start out with the familiar single watch experience. For someone who wants to take it up a notch, suggest multiview using the standard button offered by AVPlayerViewController.

rule: Use title and thumbnail previews in content browsers; minimize decorations to aid identification.
quote: Describe each piece of content succinctly with a title and thumbnail preview of the content. The browser area is limited relative to the video screens, so minimize decorations and focus on elements that facilitate identification.

rule: Keep app windows cohesive and contained; anchor controls outside but linked to the view.
quote: The content and UI of your app should be contained in a window. Controls like Tab bars and Toolbars can live outside the window, but they are still anchored to the view.

rule: Use Glass material for windows so they adapt intelligently to the user's environment lighting.
quote: Visually comfortable experiences are those that feel part of the operating system which was designed to blend with the world. Like the Glass material used for windows. Since there isn't a concept of light and dark mode on visionOS, Glass is rendered through the system and intelligently adapts to the lighting in peoples environment.

rule: Apply hover effects only to interactive elements; avoid them on read-only data to reduce confusion.
quote: Every element that's interactive and has a detail view, like hourly temperatures, uses a hover effect. But the data that is meant to be read like details around dawn and dusk, don't require a hover effect.

rule: Use at least 60 points of tap target space for interactive elements to prevent user frustration.
quote: Keep in mind, interactive elements need sufficient tap targets, so use at least 60 points of space.

rule: Use subtle animation like pulsing outlines to guide users toward the first required interaction.
quote: Notice the pulsing stroke outline around the music icon. This is a subtle way to guide you to tap on the music library. It's a simple detail with a big impact.

rule: Automate complex manual processes hidden from the user to reduce cognitive load and focus on creative tasks.
quote: In the 3D environment, we asked ourselves, 'Why a DJ would even need to manually match tempos? When we could completely automate the process under the hood?' This abstraction not only reduces complexity, but also enhances the user's ability to focus more on the creative aspects of DJing.

rule: Improve typing latency in complex code expressions to enhance developer experience and reduce friction.
quote: optimized text input in Xcode this year, improving typing latency in some complex expressions by up to 50%
finding: 50% improvement in typing latency for complex expressions

rule: Load workspaces 40% faster by optimizing initialization and resource allocation for large projects.
quote: It's now 40% faster to load a workspace. For large projects, this makes a big difference.
finding: 40% faster workspace loading

rule: Enable voice control to write code by understanding Swift syntax, spacing, operators, and camel-casing from natural speech.
quote: Voice Control understands Swift syntax. It will figure out where spaces should appear, whether expressions correspond to operators or should be camel-cased

rule: Show code changes incrementally and let users undo them by preserving snapshots before each AI-generated modification.
quote: Xcode keeps a snapshot of your code before each change is applied, so you can easily view and unwind them using the modification history

rule: Enable customization of gauge arc, start points, and end points to adapt to brand identity and hardware configurations.
quote: Circular gauges let you decide the arc of the gauge too, as well as it's start and end points

rule: Place widgets on horizontal surfaces at a gentle angle toward the viewer for legibility and grounded appearance.
quote: When placed on a horizontal surface, like a desk, table, or shelf, the widget gently tilts towards the person placing it. This subtle angle helps legibility.

rule: Offer small widget templates for productivity content that fits next to other workspace elements.
quote: If you are designing a productivity-focused widget, you might want to offer it in a small template size so it fits easily on a desk.

rule: Use extra-large widget templates for visually rich, decorative content that functions as statement pieces.
quote: if your goal is to let people decorate their space while using Vision Pro with something visually rich, like an artwork or photography, consider using the extra large template size.

rule: Allow widget resizing from 75% to 125% of base template size while preserving layout integrity.
quote: Each template size can be resized using the corner affordance, scaling from 75% to 125% while still preserving your layout.

rule: Adapt widget information density based on viewing distance using two proximity thresholds.
quote: visionOS provides two key thresholds you can design for. Default, when the widget is viewed up close, and Simplified, when it's seen from a distance.

rule: Scale interactive element targets appropriately for both close and distant viewing in proximity-aware widgets.
quote: Use proximity awareness to your advantage so that the interactive areas of your widget are always easy to target, whether someone is standing close or further away.

rule: Use gradual light modulation instead of fading for material transitions to preserve optical integrity.
quote: Instead of fading, Liquid Glass objects materialize in and out by gradually modulating the light bending and lensing, ensuring a graceful transition that preserves the optical integrity of the material.

rule: Restrict Liquid Glass to navigation layers floating above content; avoid applying it to content tables.
quote: it is best reserved for the navigation layer that floats above the content of your app. Consider this tableview: making it Liquid Glass would make it compete with other elements and muddy the hierarchy.

rule: Never stack Liquid Glass elements; use fills and transparency for overlays instead.
quote: always avoid glass on glass Stacking Liquid Glass elements on top of each other can quickly make the interface feel cluttered and confusing.

rule: Apply tinting selectively to primary actions and elements; avoid tinting all UI components.
quote: Avoid tinting all your elements. When every element is tinted, nothing stands out, and it can be confusing.

rule: Avoid intersections between scrolling content and Liquid Glass; reposition or scale content to maintain separation.
quote: In steady states, such as when an app first launches, avoid intersections between content and Liquid Glass. Instead, reposition or scale the content to maintain separation.

rule: Use scaledToFit3D modifier to maintain model aspect ratio while scaling across all three dimensions.
quote: I can use the new scaledToFit3D modifier in addition to resizable(), causing my robot to maintain the model's aspect ratio while still sizing up or down to fit the available width, height, and now depth.

rule: Customize depth alignment (front, center, back) on Layout types to position 3D views properly.
quote: Just like you can configure in HStack to align its content on the center, top, or bottom edge, you may want to configure how views are aligned in depth on visionOS.

rule: Use SpatialContainer to align multiple views in the same 3D space with 3D alignment guides.
quote: The new SpatialContainer API allows you to place multiple views in the same 3D space like a series of Nesting Dolls. You can apply a three dimensional alignment to all of the views.

rule: Use spatialOverlay to overlay a single view in the same 3D space as another with 3D alignment.
quote: spatialOverlay is a similar tool, which allows you to overlay a single view in the same 3D space as another. Similar to SpatialContainer, it supports 3D alignments.

rule: For direct-input games, combine visual and audio feedback so every contact feels satisfying; use effects like lightning streaks and impact sounds.
quote: make sure to include plenty of feedback, so every contact with an object feels satisfying for the player. You can use a combination of visual feedback, like the lightning streak behind your hand and the flying pulp. And you can add sounds, like squishing and splashing.

rule: Prefer system gestures over custom ones; players already know them, need no extra equipment, and they work across all spaces without learning overhead.
quote: players already know exactly how to use the system gestures, because they're already using them to navigate all the other apps and games on the platform. You won't need to teach them how to interact with your game. And there's no extra equipment needed.

rule: If using custom gestures, keep them sparse, simple, and intuitive; teach them during onboarding with visual and audio feedback so players learn and remember them.
quote: Any custom gestures you create for your game need to be easy for players to learn, and easy for them to remember. Make sure the gestures are a great fit for the action in your game so they'll be intuitive.

rule: Auto-detect connected game controllers and switch input handling; do not require players to find a settings menu to enable controller support.
quote: Detecting that a controller is connected, and switching your input over to work with that controller, is much better than making the player search for a switch in your game's Settings menu.

rule: Ensure all game UI and actions are accessible via game controller when one is connected; do not require system gestures for any part of the experience.
quote: make sure you can do everything in the game with the controller. Expecting players to use a system gesture to access part of your UI would be inconvenient and pretty confusing.

rule: Use Breathe animation to convey status changes or ongoing activity; Breathe modulates opacity and size for lifelike presence, unlike Pulse which uses opacity alone.
quote: Breathe is the animation that smoothly increases and decreases the presence of a symbol, giving it a living quality. It helps convey status changes, or it can signal that an activity is taking place.

rule: Use animations intentionally and sparingly; too many or misplaced animations overwhelm and distract from content and critical actions.
quote: Animations are great in UI, but using too many or in the wrong context can make it feel overwhelming and distracting, drawing attention away from important content and actions.

rule: Simplify geometry to necessary complexity; decimate distant assets to reduce computational load while maintaining perceived detail.
quote: Geometry should be as complex as necessary to communicate the asset with enough detail. As the tree asset is located at the back of the scene, and it requires less detail, so in this case, the tree asset can be decimated.

rule: Modulate four core voice qualities—clarity, simplicity, friendliness, helpfulness—by turning each up or down based on the situation to adjust tone.
quote: to help you dial in your tone for a specific situation, it can be helpful to think of each of these qualities as something that can be turned up or down

rule: Read UX writing aloud to confirm it sounds like your app's intended personality before shipping.
quote: Read your writing out loud. Ask yourself. Does this sound like the best version of your app?

rule: Write inclusively to avoid jargon that excludes people unfamiliar with specialized terminology.
quote: Avoid jargon. Not everyone knows it, so it can make people feel left out. On a related note, write inclusively.

rule: Use scroll transitions to rotate, offset, or change opacity of list elements based on their scroll position to create unique, engaging scroll experiences.
quote: Scroll transition exposes the content I'd like to transition, as well as a phase. I can use these values to change the rotation, and offset of each photo in my scroll view. Based on its position.

rule: Land people directly in the detail view at app launch by intelligently surfacing the most relevant item based on location, recency, frequency, or user intent.
quote: Land people directly in the detail view when they launch your app. Use location, recency, frequency, or some other indication of user intent to inform which detail to surface first.

rule: Design watchOS detail views to be unmistakable at a glance so they require no title for clarity.
quote: Strive to make your detail view so unmistakable at a glance that it doesn't need a title.

rule: Use full-screen color and imagery in watchOS dial-based views to add context and reduce text dependency for dense information delivery.
quote: Dial-based views are great for dense information delivered at a glance. The use of full screen color and imagery, like weather conditions, can help to add additional context.

rule: Test interactive experiences in device frequently; prototype often to validate assumptions before shipping.
quote: everything changes once you're testing in device. You may imagine how things are going to look and feel while designing, but you can't know for certain until you test them. Prototype and test your ideas in device as often as you can.

rule: Use proximity, motion, and sound to implicitly cue interaction; lead users to objects they naturally want to touch.
quote: use cues like proximity, motion, and sound to pull them in. And just make sure that your first interaction is with something small, simple, and welcoming to ease your audience in.

rule: Open your app as part of intent completion to show the user that a change has occurred in the app state.
quote: In iOS 18, opening your app is now a common behavior to show people that the intent has made a change in the app. Returning an open as part of your app intent gives people the option to see the change.

rule: Group hover effects to activate together when looking at any part of the group; use explicit or implicit grouping to control activation areas.
quote: Grouped effects are applied together, whenever any effect in the group becomes active. When effects from different views are grouped together, the group becomes active when I look at any of those views.

rule: Show only essential information on Watch widgets; people spend about ten seconds max engaging with glanceable content.
quote: people should only be spending around ten seconds max engaging with glanceable information on their Watch

rule: Use standard design layouts for Watch widgets to ensure visual consistency and smooth reading experience.
quote: visual consistency is key to providing a smooth and predictable reading experience

rule: Make widgets recognizable and distinctive by choosing background colors that convey meaning or assist app recognition.
quote: choose a color for their widget background that assists in app recognition or conveys informational meaning

rule: Prioritize widgets to appear in Smart Stack based on imminent time/date, reached location, detected headphones, sleep/wake times, or workout activity.
quote: when a time and date is imminent, when a location has been reached, when headphones are detected, when a person wakes up or when they're going to bed, or when a person starts or ends a Workout

rule: Focus app shortcuts on essential, habitual actions and content; do not fill all spaces with shortcuts.
quote: focus on the essential, habitual actions and content from your app

rule: Order shortcuts to match user's mental model and reflect decisions made inside the app to build muscle memory.
quote: order your shortcuts to reflect the decisions people make inside your app, and to help people build muscle memory

rule: Make shortcut titles concise and avoid truncation; never include app name since it is shown separately.
quote: keeping your titles concise to avoid truncation and never include your app name

rule: Use discrete symbol effects for one-off animations triggered by user events; use indefinite effects for continuous animations.
quote: Bounce, for example, plays a one-off animation on the symbol. This is considered discrete behavior. Adding a Scale effect, on the other hand, changes the symbol's scale level and keeps it there indefinitely

rule: Apply symbol animations to multiple related symbols by adding the effect on a parent view; use symbolEffectsRemoved to prevent inheritance when needed.
quote: the symbolEffect modifier propagates through the view hierarchy. This means effects can be applied to multiple images by adding the modifier on a parent view

rule: Build designs on the actual device to surface interaction details and complexity hidden in static tools.
quote: All of these details were initially opaque when we began designing. But the moment we started making prototypes, they were obvious.

rule: Use on-device demos to communicate designs more effectively than slides; demos explain themselves and build consensus.
quote: When people can hold a demo of your work in their hands, designs explain themselves. This helps build consensus and can save everyone the hassle of more meetings.

rule: Use round shapes and avoid sharp edges to guide eye focus to element centers and improve targeting accuracy.
quote: To help our eyes, use round shapes like circles, pills, and rounded rectangles. Avoid using shapes with sharp edges.

rule: Maintain a minimum target area of 60 points by combining size and spacing for eye-based interaction.
quote: The minimum area that your element needs for eye target is 60 points. But the element can be smaller than 60 points. You can achieve the minimum target area combining size and spacing.

rule: Use dynamic scaling so UI maintains the same field-of-view coverage and target area size regardless of window distance.
quote: Dynamic scale keeps your UI and the target areas at the same size, while fixed scale changes the size and makes the target areas too small.

rule: Control tip frequency so multiple tips do not appear simultaneously; stagger them across hours or days to avoid overwhelming users.
quote: The tips are all useful but would be less effective if they all showed up at once. With TipKit, I can set the display frequency for the tips, so they appear at a more ideal cadence.

rule: Dismiss tips once users perform the described action or reach maximum display count to remove outdated education.
quote: Once they see the tip and tap the favorite button, I'll call the invalidate method with the reason `.userPerformedAction` to signify that the desired outcome has been performed and the tip will be dismissed.

rule: Limit each watchOS page to single screen height to encourage focused purpose and glanceability.
quote: we advise limiting the content of an individual page to a single screen height. Embracing this constraint encourages each page to serve a clear and distinct purpose and results in a more glanceable design.

rule: Use vertical pagination instead of horizontal pagination for watchOS navigation.
quote: Use Vertical Pagination in place of horizontal pagination, which is more difficult to navigate on Apple Watch.

rule: Smoothly animate elements between pages using scale and position changes to maintain object permanence.
quote: Smoothly animate elements between pages by manipulating their scale, position, and information density, instead of introducing additional instances of that element on each page. This object permanence helps provide a visual anchor for users as they navigate through full-screen pages of content.

rule: Use background colors and content to aid navigation and app recognition, not as mere visual flourish.
quote: Background content in watchOS 10 should play a supporting role that provides additional utility, not merely be a visual flourish.

rule: Arrange important toolbar items in the trailing section to remain visible across window sizes.
quote: Arrange important toolbar items in the trailing section to avoid overflow in smaller window sizes.

rule: Group related toolbar actions to keep them together and prevent toolbar overflow.
quote: Use groups to keep related actions together in the toolbar or the overflow menu.

rule: Use horizontal submenus on iPad for quick in-place selection when screen space allows.
quote: on iPadOS 16, submenus open horizontally when they have space available. This makes them much faster, especially with a pointer.

rule: Limit app shortcuts to two to five high-quality shortcuts per app; maximum ten.
quote: in most cases, the key features of your app can be captured in two to five high-quality app shortcuts, and we strongly recommend keeping your set as focused as possible

rule: Use dynamic parameters only for finite, predictable lists of five or fewer items.
quote: you can only have one dynamic parameter in your phrase, and it can only be used to select from a finite list

rule: Use parameter confirmation to present an assumed value and ask for confirmation rather than forcing users to choose.
quote: try to make a meaningful assumption and present it as an option for people to confirm. This is called a Parameter Confirmation

rule: Use intent confirmation only for consequential actions: financial, destructive, or high-risk.
quote: only use this step for consequential actions, be it a financial transaction, a destructive action like deleting content, or an action that may just feel high risk

rule: Use custom snippets for self-contained actions; use live activities for continuous access needs like timers.
quote: If you're not sure which one to use, think about whether people would benefit from continuous access to this information, such as transit progress for a food order or a timer counting down. If so, use a Live Activity

rule: Use Automatic rendering mode for symbols; it selects the preferred rendering mode that best highlights each symbol's unique characteristics.
quote: Symbols now feature a preferred rendering mode, which can vary between symbols. And we call this behavior Automatic Rendering. When selected, it provides the preferred rendering mode configuration for each symbol without having to specify it manually

rule: Use Variable Color to represent sequential states or strength levels in symbols, not to create depth.
quote: Variable Color is not meant to create depth; instead, it's meant to highlight a sequence of steps or stages that the symbol can represent

rule: Keep tab bar persistent at bottom of screen so users can toggle between top-level content areas without losing context.
quote: Persistent access to the tab bar gives someone the ability to toggle between different levels of your information hierarchy while maintaining context in each.

rule: Never force a user to switch tabs automatically; let them choose when to navigate between tabs.
quote: Never force someone to change tabs automatically.

rule: Use clear, concise, self-evident tab labels that tell a story about app functionality without requiring users to see content first.
quote: Notice how the tabs hint at functionality. They tell a story about what the app can do just by displaying concise labels.

rule: Present modals from bottom of screen to cover tab bar and reinforce focus on a single task.
quote: When using modals on iOS, always present them from the bottom of the screen. A modal interrupts information hierarchy. It comes from the bottom of the screen to cover your tab bar.

rule: Increase Arabic font size by 10% when paired with uppercase Latin to compensate for optical size difference.
quote: you may want to increase the Arabic font size by 10%. This subtle difference would also help with legibility especially when upper case is used in smaller point sizes.
finding: 10% increase in Arabic font size compensates for optical volume difference with uppercase Latin

rule: Increase vertical spacing in UI when using vocalization marks and diacritics in Arabic to prevent text clipping.
quote: If your app would include an intense use of vocalization marks, make sure to have more vertical spacing in the UI to avoid clipping.

rule: Reduce Live Activity height dynamically when information decreases to minimize lock screen space.
quote: dynamically change the height of your Live Activity between different moments as you have more or less information to display

rule: Use numeric content transition to animate counting numbers and content-replace transition for graphic elements.
quote: Use the numeric content transition to count up or down important numbers in your Activity. And for animating in and out graphic elements and text, use the content replace transition.

rule: Remove Live Activities from lock screen after a short duration when they end to avoid manual dismissal.
quote: make sure to remove it from the lock screen after a short duration of time, as it can be annoying if it sticks around too long

rule: Keep Dynamic Island content concentric by using even margins and nesting rounded shapes inside each other.
quote: A key aspect to making things fit nicely inside the Dynamic Island is for them to be concentric with its shape. This is when rounded shapes nest inside of each other with even margins all the way around.

rule: Make Dynamic Island Compact view as narrow as possible with content snug against the sensor region.
quote: A key goal is for the encapsulation to be as narrow as possible with no wasted space. Ensure content is snug against the sensor region.

rule: Maintain relative placement of elements between Dynamic Island Compact and Expanded views for coherence.
quote: When laying out your expanded view, try and maintain the relative placement of things between the two views. That way there's a coherence between them.

rule: Place content requiring extended reading farther than arm's length and allow depth adjustment for viewer comfort.
quote: Content requiring fixating the eyes for an extended time, such as for reading, is most visually comfortable when placed farther than arm's-length distance. In addition, enable a person to adjust content depth

rule: Make moving objects semitransparent so passthrough is visible and brain interprets motion correctly.
quote: you can mitigate this by making objects semitransparent when they move, so the passthrough content is clearly visible during the motion

rule: Keep camera focus of expansion slow, predictable and within field of view to prevent motion discomfort.
quote: you want to move the camera in such a way that the motion of the focus of expansion is slow and predictable, and you want to keep the focus of expansion within the field of view

rule: Avoid oscillations at 0.2 Hz frequency; if unavoidable keep amplitude low and content semitransparent.
quote: try to avoid oscillations in general, and in particular those with frequencies around 0.2 Hz. That is one oscillation per 5 seconds. And if you really cannot avoid showing oscillating motions, try to keep the amplitude of the motion low

rule: Synchronize state changes and animations across all participants to make gestures and interactions meaningful.
quote: Your app needs to synchronize everyone's view of content, showing animations and any state changes in lockstep. This is key to making gestures like pointing make sense to everyone on the call.

rule: Allow personalized controls for accessibility while keeping main shared context identical across participants.
quote: While it's important to share as much context across devices as possible, look for opportunities for software to improve on the physical limitations of real-world social experiences, especially when it comes to comfort and accessibility.

rule: Allow individuals to open separate personal windows while maintaining shared context for group coordination.
quote: If individuals want to separately dive in on another part of the document, you could always allow each person to open a personal window, as if they brought their own iPad to the meeting.

rule: Show the correct button glyph for the controller the player is holding, even after they remap buttons in system settings.
quote: we actually want to show the X glyph when a developer asks for the glyph associated with the A action

rule: Use positional button locations instead of button names for new and young players who may not recognize button labels.
quote: Some players, especially new and young players, may more quickly recognize the location you're showing them and they don't have to glance down to try to read the button names

rule: Apply adaptive trigger resistance dynamically based on player action intensity to emulate physical sensations like rope tension.
quote: By dynamically applying a varying resistance to the trigger based on what the player is doing, you can emulate the feeling of pulling a bow string or a slingshot that's under tension

rule: Turn off adaptive trigger effects when no longer needed to prevent unexpected haptic feedback.
quote: just like I remind my kids to turn out the lights when they leave a room, you need to make sure you turn off the adaptive trigger effect when you're done

rule: Preserve the number and order of paths across all design variants when supporting multicolor or hierarchical rendering modes.
quote: Preserving the number of paths across all design variants is a requirement if you want to produce a symbol with multicolor or hierarchical data

rule: Convert live strokes to paths in symbol designs to enable colors and hierarchy groups to be applied later.
quote: Avoid using live strokes in the final design. Instead, make sure to convert any strokes to paths so that the resulting shapes can take on colors or hierarchy groups

rule: Use system-provided colors in multicolor symbols so they adapt to light mode, dark mode, high contrast, and vibrancy contexts automatically.
quote: It's recommended to use system-provided colors whenever possible, as they will adapt to changes in the system's appearance to look great in light mode, dark mode, high contrast modes, and different vibrancy contexts

rule: Keep AR experiences under two minutes to prevent user fatigue and manage battery and thermal impact.
quote: craft experiences that last no more than a minute or two. This is for the ergonomic reasons I mentioned earlier, but also because AR is a resource-intensive superpower that has a big impact on battery and thermals.
finding: experiences limited to 1–2 minutes

rule: Use screen space overlay for text and buttons rather than placing them in 3D world to preserve legibility in AR.
quote: It's best to place text and interactive elements like buttons here in screen space, rather than in the 3D world of the camera to preserve legibility.

rule: Provide real-time audio and haptic feedback as users move devices in AR to signal actions outside their view.
quote: Try to provide real-time feedback with visual effects and sound as people move, so that even if the action is taking place out of view, people can still connect with the experience.

rule: Design AR buttons for one-handed thumb use with high contrast, oversized icons at arm's length.
quote: Use oversized buttons with high-contrast icons that are easy to tap one-handed with a thumb.

rule: Use realistic shadows and lighting in AR to help virtual objects feel grounded in the scene.
quote: The quality of lighting and shadows in your experiences can have a huge impact on people's feeling that things are really there, even when an object isn't very realistic.

rule: Use Compressed width style only for single lines or display headlines; avoid for extended reading passages.
quote: the Compressed style, while still functional for small single lines, might be too tight for longer passages of text, like you see here. So always consider legibility when opting for a non-Regular Width.

rule: Pair extreme weight and width proportions for expressive display styles; center styles for neutral voice.
quote: the styles that gravitate towards the center of the stylistic map of SF to have a more neutral voice, while the styles around the perimeter of the map, which feature more extreme Weight and Width proportions, to be more expressive, have a stronger voice

rule: Use Condensed width to fit more text per line in narrow columns without sacrificing readability.
quote: the Width styles can help control longer passages of text, providing the ability to fit more characters per line, achieving a more ideal and comfortable reading experience for narrow columns.

rule: Show participant initials or names when others interact with shared content to reinforce presence and context.
quote: the app shows the initials of who drew it, and this makes for a much more intuitive experience for the entire group. It also helps reinforce the feeling of presence

rule: Provide easy access to status bar controls during immersive experiences; use a simple, discoverable gesture to redisplay hidden UI.
quote: it is important to remember that the pill in the status bar gives people access to important controls. So, let people redisplay a hidden status bar using a simple, discoverable gesture

rule: Support Picture in Picture for coordinated media so users maintain presence with the group while multitasking or switching apps.
quote: remember to support Picture in Picture for coordinated media experiences. This will allow everyone to continue watching with their friends, maintaining a sense of presence

rule: Use shared playback controls without restrictions on who can interact; everyone should feel able to control shared experiences equally.
quote: it's critical that we don't put any limitations on who can interact with these controls. We want to create an engaging experience where everyone feels like they're able to walk up and control that same music player

rule: Include descriptive metadata (title, subtitle, image, web URL) for group activities so invitees know what to expect before joining.
quote: It's important that this information is descriptive so that Ryan and Adam know what to expect when they join the SharePlay session. So be sure to implement the metadata property for your group activity with meaningful information

rule: Place the collaboration button next to the share button where it stands out and draws attention as a primary feature.
quote: This collaboration button is one of the most important UI elements of the entire collaboration experience. Find a place where it can stand out and draw people's attention. It's best to place the collaboration button right next to the share button

rule: Consolidate multiple collaboration notifications in Messages into a single banner to avoid cluttering the conversation.
quote: To not clutter conversation with too many banners, Messages will consolidate those banners into one. When people tap on the view button in this banner, Messages will show all the updates in one place

rule: Keep the collaboration popover middle section glanceable; avoid overloading with too much information or too many buttons.
quote: Try not to overload this collaboration popover with too much information or too many buttons. Keep it glanceable

rule: Anticipate the next action or question users will have and provide information or prompts in sequence to guide them.
quote: When writing for apps, you always have to ask, 'What comes next?' Anticipating the next action or question someone's going to have will help you know what to say

rule: Write button labels that describe the specific action, not generic terms like Yes or No, so users understand the choice without additional context.
quote: it's always best to be specific about the action the buttons are going to take. On this alert, if you only read the button labels, you would still understand what you were choosing

rule: Use simple, plain language avoiding idioms and culturally specific phrases that may not translate or be universally understood.
quote: It's best to use simple, plain language, as idioms and humor can be misunderstood or not translate, and some phrases have meanings that exclude people

rule: Consider context outside the app—whether users are at rest, moving, occupied with other tasks—and adjust text verbosity accordingly.
quote: When someone uses your app, are they likely to be at home in a quiet space, or traveling at busy airport? Are they occupied with something else, like driving or cooking, or can they give your app their full attention?

rule: Position on-screen instructions where users are already looking, not in arbitrary locations, to reduce cognitive load during focused tasks.
quote: An on-screen arrow guides you with instructions, to 'Move continuously when taking a Panorama.' The words appear right below the arrow because that's where you're looking

rule: Show previews before destructive or permanent actions complete, and different previews after completion.
quote: For actions that are permanent, like deletion or ordering, you should strongly consider showing a different snippet before the action is completed as compared to the one that is shown after it's completed.

rule: Use filled symbols in swipe actions and tab bars to indicate selection and emphasize active state with accent color.
quote: A filled symbol in swipe actions and iOS tab bars give a consistent appearance and level of emphasis, giving better control in areas that indicate selection when defined with an accent color.

rule: Apply hierarchical rendering (single color with varying opacity) to emphasize symbol differences when displaying multiple related symbols.
quote: When multiple symbols that share common shapes are presented alongside one another, this rendering mode emphasizes the differences between them, intending to make the symbols more legible and recognizable.

rule: Keep interactive elements centered with at least 60 points of tap target area, adding 8 points minimum spacing around smaller visual elements.
quote: Interactive elements must have a tap target area with at least 60 points of space, so they can be easily selected. This means that your UI element can be visually smaller, like the standard button, which is 44 points, as long as you add enough space around it.
finding: 60 points minimum tap target; 44-point button requires 8 points spacing

rule: Limit tab bar to six items maximum to keep the interface light and navigable.
quote: In general, you want to keep those feeling light, so avoid having more than six items.

rule: Use white text or symbols over glass material colors when color options make text visibility difficult.
quote: Colorful elements on top of the glass may be hard to see if the color of the glass is similar. Most of the time, consider using white text or symbols so they are always clearly visible.

rule: Place ornaments overlapping the bottom edge by 20 points to integrate them visually with the main window.
quote: When ornaments sit at the bottom edge of the window, place them so they overlap the bottom edge by 20 points. This helps ornaments to feel like they're integrated with the main window without blocking too much content.
finding: 20-point overlap for bottom-edge ornaments

rule: Keep UI in people's field of view; avoid placing content too high, too low, or too far down due to head rotation limits.
quote: Because of the neck's range of motion, it's easier for most people to turn their head farther to the right and to the left rather than up and down. So keep your UI in people's field of view and be careful about placing anything too high up or too far down.

rule: Use wider aspect ratios with horizontal canvas extension rather than vertical to accommodate ergonomic head movement.
quote: If you need a large canvas for your app, go with a wider aspect ratio than taller. For example, in Freeform, the canvas extends horizontally and not vertically.

rule: Randomize pitch and amplitude of repetitive sounds to feel natural rather than static over time.
quote: When you know a sound will be played often, it helps to slightly randomize some elements of the sound like its pitch and amplitude. It feels more natural and less static when keys are pressed in rapid succession.

rule: Use distance and volume together to position sounds naturally; reduce volume and push location back to avoid harsh proximity.
quote: It's way too loud and feels too close, so we need to do two things. First, turn down the volume of each a few decibels, And then push the location of the sound into the distance so it can sound further away.

rule: Animate symbols layer by layer by default to create clear, precise choreography that guides visual hierarchy.
quote: By default, a symbol will animate by layer. This means that each layer will animate one at a time, making the symbol's choreography have clear and precise movements.

rule: Use Bounce animation to confirm actions or indicate state changes; use Scale to provide focus or selection feedback.
quote: Bounce communicates that an action has occurred or that an action needs to take place. Scale, on the other hand, can provide focus or feedback when an item is selected. In addition to that, this effect is also stateful, meaning the scaled state persists until the effect is removed.

rule: Balance expressive animations with functional clarity; avoid overwhelming interfaces and prioritize the intended goal.
quote: All these new presets can serve as a communication tool between a person and the interface and have a crucial role in enhancing the user experience, but it's important to work on achieving the right balance between attention-grabbing animations and a functional interface, so that the experience doesn't result in something overwhelming.

rule: Use bar charts for comparing values across categories to enable easier relative size comparison.
quote: By making the bars horizontal, I can accentuate the difference between this chart and the recent sales chart.

rule: Use distinct colors or visual styles when displaying multiple chart types to signal differences in data.
quote: Giving each of these charts a distinct color helps. Now it is easier to notice that these charts are unique.

rule: Preserve chart values and context when linking static preview charts to expanded detailed versions.
quote: When you create a link between two versions of the same chart, that progression should maintain continuity by preserving values, context and state.

rule: Use bar marks over point or line marks when data has gaps or zeros, as bars reveal absence without distraction.
quote: Here, zeros are visible without creating a distraction. This chart is also intuitive to read: more white means more sales. Since sales are cumulative, the visual weight of all the bars corresponds directly to the number of sales made in the last 30 days.

rule: Test chart designs with real, messy data early; clean synthetic data masks interpretation problems.
quote: It's important to test your designs with real data early. While point marks are a great at revealing some insights, such as identifying outliers or clusters in data, our needs call for something else.

rule: For chart axes with no natural maximum, use dynamic ranges to let data fill available vertical space.
quote: There is no limit to how many pancakes the food trucks will sell. So let's use a dynamic range to automatically adapt the upper bound of our vertical axis to our data.

rule: Fix the lower axis bound to zero for bar charts to keep bar heights proportional to their values.
quote: We still fix the lower bound to 0. Doing so is generally a good idea when using bar marks as it keeps the heights of the bars meaningful.

rule: Use approximately four horizontal grid lines; adjust density based on context and space to balance readability.
quote: For our chart's context and intended use, it's more effective to use around four horizontal grid lines and adjust as the range of the axis changes.

rule: Use intuitive values like multiples of 20 or 7-day intervals for axis labels to aid mental math.
quote: Note that as we place these grid lines and labels, we use intuitive values to make the chart approachable– in this case, multiples of 20. In the same way, it's intuitive for people to read time in steps of seven days, which gives us five grid lines for a 30-day period.

rule: Use chart titles as headings to provide context; omit axis labels if title clarifies meaning.
quote: By using 'Pancakes sold' as a heading for the chart, the chart's meaning is front and center.

rule: Summarize the main takeaway in a title, not just the metric: include a concrete value or interpretation.
quote: Let's bring out a main take-away for our chart by rewriting our chart title to say 'Total Sales: 1,234 Pancakes'. This description grounds our chart with a concrete value and summarizes the most critical information.

rule: Order VoiceOver data labels: context (date) first, then value, to help users locate specific points.
quote: We also order the contextualizing data value, in this case, the date, to come first. This ordering makes it easier to quickly look for a specific value.

rule: Test gesture-based interactions with users who have low muscle tone to ensure the gestures require minimal energy.
quote: we needed the gesture that would expend the least amount of energy, and we started with just this pinch gesture

rule: Use machine learning on sensor data to detect subtle muscle movements, enabling gesture control for users with limited mobility.
quote: combine the accelerometer, the gyroscope, and some of those health sensors that detect heart rate, and use that to detect subtle muscle movements

rule: Present accessibility controls and visual warnings upfront so users discover them before encountering barriers.
quote: very good at presenting those controls and those warnings upfront

rule: Offer text customization settings including contrast, line spacing, and word spacing to support users with low vision or dyslexia.
quote: increase contrast or decrease contrast, space out lines, words, and highlight certain phrases

rule: Design onscreen elements to animate in direct proportion to physical user movement, creating a clear cause-and-effect relationship.
quote: look for opportunities for the onscreen elements to animate in a way that feels related to your physical movements

rule: Use haptic feedback instead of sound when the target is close; haptics communicate distance and proximity more effectively at arm's reach.
quote: the arrow defers to a form of feedback that we find much more effective at this small scale. The design transforms to highlight haptic feedback

rule: Use multiple feedback modes that are salient enough to be clearly understood; no single feedback mode should dominate or compete with the primary task.
quote: Make sure your design uses more than one mode of feedback, and that each one is salient enough to be clearly understood

rule: Automate joining shared activities; minimize required interactions before launching the experience.
quote: automate as much as you can and minimize unneeded upfront interaction before getting into the activity

rule: Use activity previews with title, subtitle, and thumbnail to provide context about shared content.
quote: Use it like a rich link, with a title, subtitle, and thumbnail to describe the experience everyone is enjoying

rule: Question every interaction and delay non-essential sign-ups or purchases in group activities.
quote: question every interaction and see if it's really necessary to get to the content and, if possible, delay or automate those interactions

rule: Design for extremes of ability and context, not just average users, across multiple diversity axes.
quote: think concretely about the extremes of how people will use the app or game, not just the average person

rule: Use constraints as creative tools to narrow problem scope and drive innovative solutions.
quote: Constraints help your process by helping you make the first few early decisions. This allows you to put most of your energy into creating new solutions in a narrow problem space

rule: Integrate accessibility and internationalization planning from the start of development, not at the end.
quote: start planning for accessibility and internationalization at the beginning of development

rule: Center perspectives at intersections of multiple diversity axes when designing inclusive features.
quote: focusing in on intersections of diversity axes is one way to not only be innovative, but respectful

rule: Use SF symbols with no localization suffix to let the system automatically adapt for the user's language and text direction.
quote: in general, you'll want to use the symbol name with no localization suffix and let the system choose the proper representation for your user's preferred language

rule: Keep achievement titles and descriptions under 30 characters for reliable display across devices.
quote: try to keep your text under 30 characters to guarantee it will work well across devices

rule: Keep leaderboard titles under 30 characters to prevent truncation across all devices and accessibility settings.
quote: keeping your leaderboard titles under 30 characters to guarantee that it will work well across all devices and accessibility settings

rule: Display unique, eye-catching artwork for each leaderboard to improve player differentiation.
quote: Ensure that you use different artwork for each leaderboard so that players can differentiate between them

rule: Use opaque circular achievement images centered, as system automatically crops to circle.
quote: provide an opaque image for each achievement. The system automatically crops the image into a circle, so make sure any primary content is centered

rule: Update color tint or provide alternate assets when Increase Contrast accessibility setting is enabled.
quote: You'll need update the tint color or provide alternate assets for high-contrast appearances
finding: Color contrast ratio of 4.5-to-1 is minimum acceptable; 7.5-to-1 greatly improves legibility

rule: Suppress parallax and motion effects when Reduce Motion accessibility setting is enabled.
quote: If you are using dramatic or frequent animations in your app, check is-Reduce-Motion-Enabled on UIAccessibility before performing them

rule: Make text wrap and avoid truncation as content size increases; use full display width available.
quote: You should avoid truncating text as the content size increases so that the user doesn't miss out on anything. Instead, wrap labels and use all of the available display width

rule: Define key repeatable user actions as intents with their necessary parameters before implementing features.
quote: determine what are the key and repeatable things that people want to accomplish. You can define these actions using what we call intents

rule: Dismiss menus by tapping outside them; do not require a dedicated cancel button.
quote: At any given time, I can tap outside the menu to dismiss it. This will hide the menu and take me back with no changes applied. It is therefore not needed to add an additional option to your menu to cancel.

rule: Position menu items smaller and more concise than action sheet items while keeping them easily tappable.
quote: The items in the menu are smaller and more concise, but still easily tappable, and they support multiple lines for longer strings.

rule: Use menus with checkmarks to show the currently selected item in selection-based interactions.
quote: Menus used for selection receive check marks next to the items that are selected.

rule: Do not hide all primary actions in a menu; keep frequently used actions prominently displayed.
quote: Hiding all actions in a menu is definitely not an approach we encourage. It hides primary actions behind an additional tap, and it doesn't give you a good understanding of what this view can do for you.

rule: Design intelligence as an adaptive, evolving platform convention that changes with user behavior, not static like icons.
quote: Unlike other forms of design, intelligence isn't a static glyph or icon like the 'share' button. It's alive. It manifests itself by adapting to how the system, the platform, conforms to how people use their devices.

rule: Help users accomplish their core job; view intelligence as a design practice that enables familiar patterns.
quote: What's the core job of a designer? It's to help people accomplish something. And one of the key ways a designer enables this is by leveraging the familiar.

rule: Use questions in voice dialogue to signal you expect an answer and need information to continue.
quote: Questions are a great conversational marker. They let people know you're expecting an answer, so be sure to use them when people need to provide information to continue.

rule: Match pointer precision to interface precision; reduce pointer precision for low-precision controls like buttons.
quote: This concept of dynamically adjusting the precision of the pointer to match the precision of the interface is called, Adaptive Precision.

rule: Require confirmation for destructive or high-consequence actions, especially for users with motor impairments.
quote: Make sure you confirm any destructive behaviors or high-consequence behaviors in your applications. This is especially important for Switch Control users who may be more likely to mistap an item.

rule: Limit small widgets to maximum four pieces of information to avoid overcrowding.
quote: We recommend only including a max of four pieces of information in the small widget size.

rule: Use 16-point layout margins for all widget sizes to maintain consistent spacing with adjacent widgets.
quote: follow the default sixteen point layout margins across all sizes to make sure the content in your widget feels consistent when it's place next to other widgets

rule: Use 11-point margins for layouts with graphical shapes like circles and inset platters to maintain tighter alignment.
quote: For layouts with graphical shapes like circles and inset platters use tighter eleven point margins across all sizes

rule: Deep-link small widgets to relevant content with a single tap target; medium and large widgets support multiple tap targets.
quote: The small widget supports a single tap target. Tapping it should deep link to the content that's on the widget.

rule: Apply weight compensation when scaling symbols to maintain consistent stroke thickness across small, medium, and large scales.
quote: we make some weight compensations which allow us to maintain the same stroke thickness making the symbols look weight matched not only between the scales but also with text

rule: Never specify fixed frames for symbols; instead use text styles and point sizes so symbols resize with Dynamic Type.
quote: Symbols are not designed to be constrained in frames with a specific size. It's the typographic nature of symbols that really makes it easy to spec, as if they were text.

rule: Use center alignment for symbols rather than aspect fit or scale to fit to maintain optical balance.
quote: make sure to use center alignments rather than aspect fit or scale to fit. And check your content gravity is set to centered

rule: Remove nonessential UI that requires precise location data when users share only approximate location instead.
quote: remove nonessential UI that requires precise data

rule: Show location-sharing status prominently on first launch, then reduce visual prominence after user interaction to balance transparency without distraction.
quote: status appears larger and stronger in visual treatment. This reminds them of past decisions and gives them direct access to control of the setting. Once people show interest and interact elsewhere in the app, the visual treatment reduces in prominence.

rule: Use gender-neutral language and pronouns; avoid binary gender references in copy and default avatars.
quote: instead of using the binary pronouns "he" or "she" in your copy, you can replace this language with the gender-neutral pronoun "they" instead

rule: Design interface functionality to support diverse family structures instead of assuming fixed roles; let users define relationships.
quote: instead of assuming there are fixed family roles, I can label each profile something neutral, like "family member." And instead of assuming how many people make up a family

rule: Craft App Clip card subtitles to explain what the App Clip does; assume users have no prior knowledge of your brand.
quote: they might not know what your name means. They're gonna need an explanation of what it is that your App Clip is there to do, and that's what you can put in the subtitle

rule: Use photographs or custom graphics for App Clip card headers; avoid screenshots and dense text as they are hard to read in small spaces.
quote: You should never use screenshots or fill it up with lots of text since both of those can be really hard to read in the small space available

rule: Launch App Clips into the specific feature or context the user needs; skip unnecessary navigation steps when context is already clear.
quote: Etsy would launch right into the part of their App Clip for the product being shown in Safari below. That saves people from having to navigate back to that product

rule: Use Apple Pay and Sign in with Apple in App Clips to reduce friction and enable seamless authentication and payment.
quote: Consider using technologies like Apple Pay and Sign in with Apple for a more seamless experience

rule: Enable interaction through gestures using minimal muscle effort: pinch, double pinch, clench, double clench for complete device access.
quote: pinch, double pinch, clench, and double clench for complete access to the Apple Watch

rule: Combine hardware sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, heart-rate) with machine learning to detect subtle muscle movements for gesture recognition.
quote: combine the accelerometer, the gyroscope, and some of those health sensors that detect heart rate, and use that to detect subtle muscle movements in your arm

rule: Vary feedback frequency based on accessibility mode: increase repetition (laughs) when VoiceOver is on; decrease when off.
quote: When VoiceOver is on, Mickey laughs more often. When VoiceOver is not on, Mickey doesn't laugh quite as much

rule: Use CSS environment variables (safe-area-inset-top, -right, -bottom, -left) to dynamically position content clear of notches and tab bars.
quote: env(safe-area-inset-bottom) is a measurement of however many pixels it is from the safe area to the bottom of the viewport

rule: Apply viewport-fit=cover in meta viewport to extend content to screen edges; use environment variables to prevent data loss in safe areas.
quote: I can signal to Safari that I want the browser to extend the content to the left and right edges by changing the meta viewport tag to viewport-fit=cover

rule: Place tab bar at bottom of iOS screen, within thumb reach for one-handed use; minimize it on scroll to preserve content space.
quote: we've moved the tab bar to the bottom of the screen. This puts it directly under the user's thumb, making it easier for them to reach, especially if they're using their phone one-handed

rule: Declare fallback theme-color first, then dark-mode variant; browsers without media-attribute support use the first declaration.
quote: put your fallback first, not last, the way you do in CSS

rule: Use page title in browser tab to surface content, not site name; place content first to aid tab identification in multi-tab sessions.
quote: put the content title first. That way, if someone has your site open in multiple tabs, it's easier to tell which tab is which

rule: Provide transparent-background favicon to maintain clarity and appearance in high-resolution devices and Safari tab bar.
quote: A favicon with a transparent background can look especially great

rule: Use Flexbox or CSS Grid to create layouts where content below a tab bar hugs the bar as it expands; content above stays fixed.
quote: the chat area is the area that resizes when the tab bar is expanded. Everything above it stays the same size, while everything below it hugs the tab bar. This is because we're using Flexbox layout

rule: Prioritize and display essential features immediately visible on the main screen; hide non-critical features behind navigation.
quote: The essential parts of your app should be immediately visible to people. It's okay for the non-essential parts to require some navigation to reach

rule: Avoid hamburger menus for primary navigation; use visible tab bars or alternatives so users see available sections at a glance.
quote: when the hamburger menu is closed, people don't know what's inside. The three lines don't convey anything about the features inside

rule: Limit tab bar buttons to 3–5; exceeding this reduces tappable area, increases visual complexity, and obscures features.
quote: too many tabs reduces the tappable area of each tab and increases the complexity of your app, which can make it harder for people to locate information

rule: Add text labels to icons to clarify ambiguous actions; camera icon can mean photo, scan document, or scan QR code without context.
quote: Even the camera icon that we are familiar with could have many possible uses, such as taking a picture, scanning a document or a QR code. When we add text labeling the button "New," we clarify this button is for capturing toast to add a new recipe

rule: Guide search entry by showing example inputs (ingredients, places, friends) to overcome blank-page paralysis and discoverability.
quote: we decided to provide examples of possible types of input, such as searching by ingredients, places, or friends. In this way, people can quickly discover different methods for how to search

rule: Use standard platform gestures (tap, swipe, long press, pinch, rotate); custom gestures mimic real-world interactions or remain invisible shortcuts.
quote: use the accepted gesture for the platform. If you're inventing a new gesture, try to mimic real-life interactions

rule: Organize content into categories matching user behavior and real-world context, not just available data; group by restaurants, friends, preferences.
quote: organize the content of your app into categories that fits people's motivation and natural behavior

rule: Visually separate content categories with header titles and spacing; grouping reduces overwhelm and clarifies existing divisions.
quote: By grouping the categories into different logical sections, separated by a header title, it feels immediately more understandable. People can easily ignore one category and explore deeper in one specific section

rule: Invite explicit user feedback on content (like, hide, flag); clear invitations increase feedback rate and feed recommendation engines useful training data.
quote: If you clearly invite people to provide feedback, they are more likely to give feedback. This will feed the recommendation engine's useful data that will reinforce relevant items and discoverability of the content

rule: Use a More button (ellipsis in circular container) for secondary actions in glanceable, non-scrolling views.
quote: So, we've added another button in the bottom right with the ellipsis glyph in the app's key color that can present these actions. This is known as a More button.

rule: Place action buttons at the bottom of detail views, applying only to the content above them.
quote: Action buttons at the bottom of a detail view may be the most discoverable and intuitive way to show actions in your app.

rule: Use the toolbar button API sparingly, only in scrolling views for essential actions not primary to the view.
quote: Only use it in a scrolling view. Scrolling is what makes this button discoverable. And use it judiciously, only for actions that are essential to the functioning of your app, but may not be the primary action for the view.

rule: Apps sharing suggestions experience 100% increase in sharing when users engage with first suggestion.
quote: when a user engages on their first Sharing Suggestion for your app, they will, on average, share twice as much as they did before through your app.
finding: 100% increase in sharing behavior after first engagement

rule: Integrate Siri Event Suggestions for actions like check-in; airlines saw 82% of check-ins come through this.
quote: Some airlines shared with us that they saw 82% of notification check-ins come from their Siri Event Suggestion check-in action.
finding: 82% of check-ins originate from Siri Event Suggestions

rule: Expose app actions through system entry points; third-party apps appear five times daily via these channels.
quote: Some third-party apps are seen, on average, five times every day on the lock screen, in Sharing, in Search, and other entry points throughout the system.
finding: 5x daily visibility increase through system entry points

rule: Use NSSearchToolbarItem to collapse search into a button when window space is constrained.
quote: When the window is large enough, the full search field is shown as normal, but when the window is compressed down, the search field is collapsed down into a button.

rule: Apply inset style to table views for improved readability: add horizontal and vertical padding around selections.
quote: The inset style applies some extra horizontal padding around your cell views and vertical padding around the top and bottom rows.

rule: Never auto-play video without checking the user's motion auto-play setting; respect accessibility preferences for motion.
quote: Auto-play video previews starts as enabled by default, but you can turn it off at any time. And, additionally, we've made this public API.

rule: Do not use color alone to convey meaning; add additional visual indicators like shapes, symbols, or text for users with color-vision deficiency.
quote: any place in my app where I use color as the only way of conveying information, I should now add some additional indicator. For example, a shape.

rule: All apps must support Dark Mode; users expect it when their device is set to Dark Mode.
quote: In general, all of your apps should support Dark Mode. When the people using your app have set their device to be in Dark Mode, they'll expect your app to change as well.

rule: Use semantic colors from the system palette instead of hardcoded color values to support both Light and Dark modes automatically.
quote: instead of maintaining two separate lists of colors for Light and Dark Modes, you can apply semantic colors from the system palette to UI elements and their appearance will automatically adapt

rule: Achieve a contrast ratio of 4.5 to 1 or higher for tint colors between Light and Dark modes using a color contrast calculator.
quote: aim for a contrast ratio of 4.5 to 1 or higher. Strong color contrast improves the accessibility and usability of your apps.
finding: 4.5:1 contrast ratio minimum

rule: Use vibrancy rather than solid colors over system materials to maintain contrast and legibility regardless of background context.
quote: With system materials, it's typically best to use vibrancy rather than solid colors. Because depending on the background context, solid colors can get really muddy and can lead to some serious legibility issues.

rule: Allow users to dismiss card-style modal sheets by swiping down anywhere on screen; implement swipe-to-dismiss as the primary dismissal method.
quote: Card-style modal sheets can be dismissed by swiping down anywhere on the screen. And that dismiss gesture is often going to be easier than tapping a button in the navigation bar.

rule: Use navigation bars without background or shadow by default to allow titles to connect seamlessly with content, fading in the background and shadow when content scrolls underneath.
quote: By default, they're now drawn for large titles without the background and shadow. This allows the title to connect seamlessly with the content that it's labeling. When content scrolls underneath the navigation bar, the background and shadow will fade back in.

rule: Specify symbols using typographic points like text, not screen dimensions, to ensure proper rendering at all sizes.
quote: They're specified in typographic points, like text.

rule: Design symbol weights to maintain detail and visibility across the full weight range from ultra-light to black.
quote: Every weight has been drawn manually, and special consideration went into each design. Thinner weights have a distinctive, beautiful elegance, while the heavier ones strive to maintain detail and visibility.

rule: Keep 5 to 10 items maximum in carousel-style content discovery to avoid noise and cognitive overload.
quote: Too many items in the Top Shelf just adds noise and clutter. So we think a good number to keep in mind is somewhere between 5 and 10.

rule: Deliver carousel images at 1920 by 1080 points filling the entire frame for full-screen content display.
quote: Content in the Top Shelf Carousel is full screen. So your images should be 1920 by 1080 points and they should draw in the entire frame of that content.

rule: Match haptic sharpness and intensity to the physical properties and velocity of on-screen objects and actions.
quote: We choose a transient event with high sharpness. We also modulate the intensity to match the velocity of the bounce.

rule: Keep suggested voice command phrases to three or fewer words, using proper nouns or verb-object patterns only.
quote: keep it short, at around three or fewer words. Try limiting it to a proper noun, or just a verb and an object.

rule: Test voice dialog repeatedly before shipping; discard dialog that becomes irritating after ten repetitions.
quote: Listen to Siri speak your dialog. How does your dialog feel to you after the third time hearing it? What about the 10th?

rule: Avoid first-person pronouns in voice dialog because users may misattribute agency to Siri rather than the app.
quote: Avoid using first-person pronouns, since Siri isn't performing the action, your app is.

rule: Present option lists upfront with phrased prompts using which-questions to minimize disambiguation steps in voice flows.
quote: You can minimize disambiguation prompts, which add another step to your conversation, by presenting an option list up front.

rule: Provide pronunciation hints for voice options to avoid verbosity, reading only differentiating details aloud.
quote: you can separately specify how Siri reads your options out loud, by providing pronunciation hits that you can add to each option.

rule: Collect training data intentionally to reflect the experience you want, not just the world as it exists; optimize for customers you want, not those you have.
quote: You shouldn't reflect the world as it is. You should reflect a better world, that world that you want it to be.

rule: Categorize and analyze ML model failures by scenario; some need better models, others need design or non-ML solutions.
quote: Group failure cases into categories and scenarios. This will help you understand how important each scenario is. Decide if it's best handled by a non-ML approach

rule: Treat metrics as proxies for abstract values like customer happiness; evolve them when they diverge from actual user experience.
quote: Metrics provide numbers, a sense of scientific accuracy, and it's easy to get caught up in numbers and improving them but we ultimately care about abstract concepts.

rule: Detect pause in finger motion by measuring acceleration, not velocity thresholds or timers.
quote: We look at your finger's acceleration. It turns out there's a huge spike in the acceleration of your finger when you pause.

rule: Animate button state changes instantly or very quickly to feel responsive; slow fades make interactions feel unresponsive.
quote: if we are going to animate it do it very quickly

rule: Allow users to drag a finger outside a button to cancel activation before release; this makes interactions feel undecided and fluid.
quote: I can actually drag my finger outside of the button to begin canceling it. This is something that's actually very important for all sorts of fluid interactions because it's what makes a fluid interaction undecided.

rule: Make the hit area of small controls larger than the visual size to aid interaction, especially for fingers.
quote: the hit area of this button might not be what you expect, if you look closely at the circle maybe I'm not quite touching it. But perhaps the hit area is actually a little bit larger than the visual size, this is particularly important for very small controls

rule: Make every notification serve a specific purpose with real, meaningful information; never use notifications just to drive app launches.
quote: Everything you said in a notification has got to be meaningful. Every notification should provide a specific purpose. Each notification should have a specific message to communicate or a task to complete. Notifications are not just a reason to get people to launch into your app.

rule: Use transient haptics for momentary impacts; use continuous haptics for sustained feedback lasting over time.
quote: We can play these continuous experiences. We can also have something that's more shorter and compact. It's a single cycle, and we call this experience a transient.

rule: Design audio-haptic feedback to match the visual animation's energy, pace, and emotional tone.
quote: Think about the pace, the energy level, and the different quality that you're trying to convey in your app. Design feedback that tell the consistent and unified story.

rule: Add audio and haptic feedback only to the most significant interactions; remove feedback that doesn't enhance value or communicate importance.
quote: Utility is about adding audio and haptic feedback only when you can provide clear value and benefit to your app experience. Use moderation. Don't add sound and haptics just because you can.

rule: Constrain pointer movement along axes to guide users toward target rows or columns, creating magnetic alignment.
quote: constrain the pointer's movement on the vertical axis. If we're using the guide, return the crosshair with the constrainedAxes set to "vertical."

rule: Extend pointer region padding beyond control bounds so pointer snaps to targets before reaching their visual edges.
quote: providing expanded padding around views to amplify the pointer's magnetism and make it easier to interact with important elements

rule: Coordinate pointer region transitions seamlessly across adjacent controls by providing contiguous regions without gaps.
quote: providing the interaction with contiguous pointer regions. When coordinating multiple pointer regions or styles, it often makes sense to take your interaction up to a higher level in the view hierarchy

rule: Show navigation alongside content simultaneously on iPad instead of in overlays or modals to maintain context during interaction.
quote: showing content along with your navigation also helps in other ways too. For example, if you want to switch between different parts of your photo library, to your albums or to all of your photos, it's now just a single tap away.

rule: Avoid modal overlays on iPad; instead keep controls at the same level as content so users see results and context simultaneously.
quote: see if you have any modal sheets or popovers, and see if those modal sheets and popovers are giving people useful context or if they're blocking other parts of your app. See if it would work better if your controls are at the same level, rather than an overlays.

rule: Move controls from iPad bottom edge to Mac toolbar to prevent them from being hidden below the dock.
quote: If your iPad app has any actions that are located along the bottom edge of the screen, doing the same thing in a Mac window can be very problematic. Mac windows are draggable. The bottom edge of Mac windows might be dragged out of you, or below the dock.

rule: Avoid small text styles like caption and footnote on Mac; bump up text size to remain legible after 77% scaling.
quote: Using some of the smallest size like footnote, caption one, caption two, can make text that's difficult to read on Mac. Even the Mac size mini is often too small. So, just -- you may find that you need to bump up text a little bit to keep it legible on Mac.

rule: Use 16-bit color depth instead of 8-bit when creating Display P3 assets to reduce visible banding in gradients.
quote: 16 bit per channel instead of the usual 8. That allows you to represent more colors within the wide gamut, which is especially useful for gradients.
finding: 16-bit Display P3 makes banding much less visible compared to 8-bit sRGB gradients

rule: Save Display P3 assets as PNG using Save As in Photoshop to embed color profiles and maintain color depth.
quote: it is key then to use Save As and PNG as your format because this is the only way at the moment to both imbed a color profile and maintain the color depth

rule: Use Convert to Profile rather than Assign to Profile when converting existing assets to Display P3 to preserve design intent.
quote: Do not use Assign to Profile as that will take your existing colors and stretch those out into the new color space changing your design

rule: Apply Display P3 selectively to apps with vibrant imagery, nature scenes, or products where color accuracy matters, not to calm desaturated designs.
quote: Display P3 works great in some cases, in others it's just not the right choice. For example, if your app is designed with a calm, de-saturated color scheme, it doesn't use a lot of imagery, display P3 might not be the right choice

rule: Design iMessage apps to feature only core communication-focused features, not replicate the entire main app experience.
quote: Tumblr, Dunkin Donuts and Tinder do not set out to put their entire apps into messages, and thankfully they didn't. They integrated only features that were focused on communication.

rule: Enable users to create and customize content within iMessage apps to increase engagement and discovery of new use cases.
quote: Handcrafted messages are fun to send and receive. Find ways to let your users create and customize the experience. You may find that there are ways to use your app that you never even imagined.

rule: Choose terms that translate similarly across languages to improve multilingual clarity; for example use photo rather than picture.
quote: When terms can be used more or less interchangeably in your app's primary language is there one choice that's very similar to other languages. For example, picture and photo are more or less the same in English, but look at the difference in these other languages. Photo is the clear winner for multilingual clarity.
