rule: Lead with content first to demonstrate app value; show features and benefits before asking for commitments or permissions.
quote: Always lead with great content. Show off what makes your app great right off the bat and let people dig in.

rule: Request permissions on an as-needed basis in context; immediately show the benefit when asking for access to user data.
quote: The app requests permissions on a need to know basis. So you retain a sense of control over both the experience and your private data.

rule: Teach app mechanics through interactive experiences rather than static onboarding; embed learning into the early gameplay or task flow.
quote: If your app requires a bit of upfront education, it's going to be a lot more compelling if it's interactive and gives people that sense of jumping right in.

rule: Apply readability margins on larger screens to restrict line length; allow text size to adjust based on Dynamic Type settings without compromising layout.
quote: If you're using Dynamic Type with readability margins, then people using your app will have a much more comfortable reading experience.

rule: Reuse standard UIKit elements (TableViews, navigation, tab bars) across iOS device sizes to maintain consistency and inherit accessibility features automatically.
quote: We have a bunch of standard UI elements that you can use in your app that will automatically adapt on all screen sizes.

rule: Normalize line weight across all glyphs in a set; consistent stroke width creates visual cohesion and prevents glyphs from appearing emphasized unevenly.
quote: Because they don't share a consistent line weight, some look more emphasized than others, and this can be confusing, and they just don't family well.

rule: Apply optical positioning adjustments to asymmetrical glyphs; mathematically centered art may need pixel adjustments to appear visually balanced.
quote: Notice, that art is perfectly centered within that space, but optically, it just, it just looks off. So, if we nudge that over a few pixels to the right, we achieve a much more balanced result.

rule: Use custom UI, typography, and visualizations in notification long looks to match your app's design language.
quote: if you have custom UI, custom typography, elements that make your app unique, you should add them here

rule: Update notification content in real time when displaying live data like maps, stock prices, or social feeds.
quote: you can update the content of a Long Look in real time. So any case where you're using a map, that is a nice example.

rule: Include 1–3 relevant quick action buttons in notifications to let users complete tasks without launching the app.
quote: at the bottom of the notification there can be some optional Quick Actions. So if it relates to the notification, add some relevant buttons.

rule: Test prototypes on the target device in realistic contexts, not in abstract or vacuum settings.
quote: show your prototypes in context, on the device they're meant for, in a somewhat realistic situation. You can't test things in a vacuum.

rule: Gather feedback on prototypes without defending, arguing, or dismissing user observations and suggestions.
quote: Don't argue, defend, or dismiss the feedback you get.

rule: Place a dominant call-to-action button (Play, Start, Battle) most prominently in busy main menu UIs with news, tournaments, and stores.
quote: game Main Menus have become increasingly busy with news, tournaments, stores, and more. And these can all be on your interface, but make sure that the main call to action to play, start, battle, or begin a new game is the most dominant in your Main Menu UI.

rule: Keep tutorial directions short, simple, and single-action; avoid repeating directions to respect player intelligence.
quote: keep directions short and simple to be effective. So, whether you teach with a character or through in-game instructional text, a single clear direction is going to be the most effective. And please, don't repeat directions.

rule: Avoid bouncing arrows and floating hand tutorials; use animation or learn-by-play instead for more effective and immersive teaching.
quote: One of the least effective ways to teach is with a bouncing arrow. It's not effective because people just end up playing tap the pointing arrow game and not learning. And the same goes for the floating hand.

rule: Ensure all interactive elements meet a minimum 44×44 point tap target size on iOS to prevent user frustration.
quote: make sure that everything that's interactive on your game's interface meets the minimum tap targets on iOS which is 44 by 44 points.

rule: Test app icons at multiple sizes, in folders, and next to other icons to ensure clarity and recognizability at small scales.
quote: examine on the Home screen, in a folder, and if your app has settings, the settings app

rule: Help users understand where they are, where they can go, and how to exit by answering these questions on every screen.
quote: every screen in your app should answer all of these questions, or else people will feel lost

rule: Provide immediate, clear, and understandable feedback for all user actions to build confidence and prevent errors.
quote: feedback that cars provide must be clear, immediate, and understandable

rule: Surface critical status information at higher levels of hierarchy to avoid forcing users to navigate deeper.
quote: surface key status information at higher levels whenever possible

rule: Make notification sounds unobtrusive and repeatable by testing them over a week to ensure they do not become annoying with frequent use.
quote: If after a week you still like the sound, it's probably a pretty good one

rule: Synchronize sound design with haptics and animation to create a cohesive multisensory experience that reinforces user perception.
quote: combining sounds and haptics the right way and synchronizing them precisely, we can come up with this great multisensory experience

rule: Increase letter spacing as point size decreases to maintain comfortable reading experiences at smaller sizes.
quote: For optical reasons, reading stays comfortable if the space between letters increases as the point size decreases. Adobe Caslon Pro has looser spacing and this contributes to a nicer reading experience at smaller size.

rule: Create typographic contrast through size, weight, or style to guide attention and establish hierarchy in layouts.
quote: The key element is typographic contrast. Whether I did it through size, weight, or style.

rule: Show working prototypes or videos to stakeholders instead of static mockups to communicate intent and spark conversations about constraints.
quote: More often than not, demonstrating with a video or a small interactive prototype can be extremely valuable in communicating the intent or better yet, sparking a conversation on constraints, possible solutions, and next steps.

rule: Load only the minimum assets needed to reach the first interactive screen, then load remaining content asynchronously.
quote: Load just enough of your assets so that you can get up and running to your first interactive screen. And then use technologies like Grand Central Dispatch, and so on, to move work off of your main thread

rule: Introduce new game mechanics one at a time during onboarding, with coaching tips shown in context as each interaction becomes relevant.
quote: once the player has that down, then they start introducing new interactions one at that time. So each time there's another coaching tip

rule: Create multiple distinct prototypes in parallel before committing to one direction; explore the entire design space with sketches before adding realism.
quote: you should not start prototyping from just a single idea. You want to explore and understand the whole space in order to figure out the best direction

rule: When testing prototypes with users, ask three questions: whether they understand how to perform the key interaction, whether it feels easy, and how they would improve it.
quote: we want to ask them three questions as we're showing them. Do you know how to do this one particular thing that we have prototyped? Is it easy to do that thing? And in general, how can we make this better?

rule: Zoom to the actual device size while prototyping to verify that text, images, and touch targets remain readable and tappable at real scale.
quote: remember to zoom out to the physical size of the device that your screen is going to live on. It's really easy to get caught up working at a zoom level where everything is big, and clear, and legible

rule: Identify which features matter most to users and your goals before designing; exclude features that don't serve either.
quote: Identify the features that matter most to the people who will use your app, and the features that serve your own goals for the app itself, in order to determine what your app should do.

rule: Learn user preferences implicitly from their behavior and interactions, not only explicit settings.
quote: By observing and responding to people's interactions or behaviors, your app can make subtle but significant adjustments to better accommodate the preferences of the people who use it.

rule: Use menus for contextual actions and view preferences, not critical-path actions needed to progress.
quote: Critical path actions, meaning actions that are necessary for the user to continue forward in your app and complete a task, should not be displayed in a menu. They should be presented in line.

rule: Use progressive loading so users reach new pages immediately instead of waiting for all content.
quote: You don't need to make people wait for all of the content to be ready to display on a page before you let them go to that page. You can bring them to the page, show a few things, and then show the rest of the stuff as it becomes available.

rule: Avoid transparency in graphics unless compositing requires it; alpha channels increase file size.
quote: Transparency requires alpha channels, and alpha channels take up file size. So avoid those unless you actually need it.
